chapters.title: Chapter 371: City Of Stars...
paragraphs: Antarctica had taught him many things. Strength was one of them.
Next time, he intended to be strong enough that survival wouldn’t need to depend upon luck or the contents of the System Shop.
Shaking his head, Stan forced those thoughts from his mind and returned his attention to the mirror before him.

The skin along his chest and arms was flawless in the specific way that skin was only flawless in photographs or on the cover of a fashion magazine. Every small imperfection he had lived with since adolescence had quietly disappeared. The small scar along his ribs from a childhood bike accident had been smoothed away entirely, while the faint stress lines that had begun gathering at the corners of his eyes over the past year of life in Wanhai simply weren’t there anymore.

The line of his shoulders was cleaner. The definition along his stomach was sharper and more pronounced without appearing unnatural, every muscle seeming perfectly proportioned as though sculpted by an obsessive artist. Even his complexion appeared healthier than before.

His hair, still a little longer than he usually wore it, fell across his forehead with the small annoying wave it had always possessed, though now it somehow seemed to obey gravity in a slightly more cinematic manner.
For a moment, he simply stared at himself in silence.
If someone had shown him this reflection a month ago and claimed it was him, he would have assumed it had been edited beyond recognition.
He looked better than he ever had in his entire life.
No, better wasn’t quite the right word.
He looked like an edited, perfected version of himself, as though someone had taken every good feature he possessed and quietly refined it to the absolute limit without changing who he was.
It was still unmistakably Stan Harrison standing before the mirror, but at the same time, it almost didn’t feel entirely real.

His strength had increased. His body had changed. He had walked through Antarctica, survived things that should have remained nothing more than myths and conspiracy theories, inherited an ancient Sovereign’s legacy, and come frighteningly close to death more than once.
Sometimes, it was difficult to believe that all of that had happened within the span of a few short weeks.
His lips curved into a faint smile before he shook his head helplessly.
His life had become absurd a long time ago.
And somehow, he had a feeling things were only just beginning.
He was not sure how he felt about that.

Sighing softly, he turned on the shower. The rainhead came alive with the low, steady rush of pressurized water striking stone, the specific sound of a modern shower running at full pressure, a soft, continuous roar that would carry through a closed door into a quiet apartment with the ease of any other sustained mechanical noise.
Stan stepped in and ler water hit him.
He closed his eyes and simply, for a moment, stood beneath it.

The warmth slowly washed away the lingering exhaustion buried deep within his muscles. The past several days had been absurd even by the increasingly ridiculous standards his life had begun to operate on. Antarctica. Ancient inheritances. Near-death experiences. Cultivation techniques. Werewolves. An ancient Royal Blood vampire currently sitting in his living room.
Sometimes, saying it aloud made it sound even more unbelievable.
He exhaled quietly and allowed himself to relax for the first time since returning home.
For now, everything else could wait.
In the living room, Camilla lifted her head very slightly at the sound.
The soft, continuous rush was, unmistakably, water.
It sounded like a small waterfall.

But it was not the sound she associated with any form of bathing she had ever experienced, not the small, polite sluice of a servant pouring from a jar over the shoulders of a bathing noblewoman, not the deep, slow lap of an ornate cultivator’s bathing pool, nor the crisp splash of a mountain stream diverted through an ancient stone channel.
It was steady. Endlessly, evenly, unhurriedly steady.
Like a waterfall.
As though some artifact hidden within the walls had, upon command, opened a permanent channel to a river and simply allowed that river to run for as long as it was asked to.
Her red eyes narrowed very slightly.
’What have they built?’ she wondered. ’What form of small, clever mechanism produces such a flow on such demand from the wall of a private residence?’
The more time she spent among modern humanity, the stranger they became.

They possessed neither spirit veins nor cultivation arts worthy of mention, and yet they had somehow filled their cities with countless small miracles that most cultivators of ancient times would have found absurd.

They had conquered the sky without wings, spoken across continents through small rectangles of glass and metal, preserved food for months within cold boxes that consumed neither ice nor spiritual energy, and illuminated entire cities brighter than the stars themselves without so much as a formation engraved upon the ground.
Humanity was, she had slowly begun to realize, extraordinarily clever.
Dangerously so. She stood in the middle of the living room and listened for another moment.

The instinct rose within her before she consciously registered it, the small, automatic pulse of a cultivator of her rank preparing to extend her spirit sense through the intervening walls to observe the mechanism directly. The same spirit sense she had extended across an entire continent of ice not twenty-four hours ago, cataloguing the werewolf pack, every scientific outpost, and every part of the surface for hundreds of kilometers in every direction.
She caught the instinct at the very edge of forming.
A small pale flush rose along the line of her jaw.

She had, in her hurry to satisfy her curiosity, been approximately half a heartbeat away from casually extending her spirit sense into the bathroom of a man who was, she reminded herself with the small, offended dignity of a woman who prided herself on never being caught uncomposed, currently inside it and decidedly unclothed.
The flush deepened by exactly one shade.

’What am I even thinking?’ she scolded herself very firmly in the private courtroom of her own thoughts. ’My intention was entirely to observe the mechanism. The mechanism. I have observed a great many things in my lifetime and I am not about to disgrace myself by fumbling my discretion over a bathroom in an apartment.’
She paused briefly before adding, somewhat less confidently,
’A very fascinating mechanism, admittedly.’
There was absolutely no reason for her curiosity to extend any further than that.
None whatsoever.
She turned very deliberately away from the direction of the bathroom.
She walked, with what she considered admirable composure, towards the tall glass wall overlooking the city beyond the penthouse.
The sight before her was beautiful in a way entirely different from the world she remembered.
No towering immortal mountains draped in clouds. No ancient palaces suspended amongst the heavens. No spirit rivers flowing across floating continents.

Instead, there were countless lights stretching endlessly towards the horizon like stars scattered across the earth itself. Glass towers pierced the night sky while the distant glow of countless vehicles flowed through the streets below like rivers of light.
Humanity had built its own stars. For all their weakness as individuals, there was something strangely magnificent about that.
The soft sound of the shower continued quietly in the background, unhurried, endless, and cheerfully unaware of the small internal argument taking place in the middle of the living room.
After a moment, having successfully redirected herself, Camilla permitted a more measured thought to surface.
’When he is finished, I will bathe as well,’ she decided solemnly. ’I shall inspect the mechanism directly. In person. From within the room. As a civilized observer.’
After all, firsthand observation was the foundation of proper scholarship.
There was nothing strange about that.
She nodded once to herself. Composure restored.
Her gaze returned to the magnificent city stretching before her as a small smile unknowingly found its way onto her lips.
The world had changed far more than she had imagined she thought, it’s nothing like her ancestors said it was...
And perhaps that was not such a terrible thing after all.

The skin along his chest and arms was flawless in the specific way that skin was only flawless in photographs or on the cover of a fashion magazine.
Every small imperfection he had lived with since adolescence had quietly disappeared.

The line of his shoulders was cleaner.

Even his complexion appeared healthier than before.

chapters.title: Chapter 372: Shameless
paragraphs: In the shower, Stan tipped his head back under the rainhead and let three days of Antarctic ice and werewolf blood and Void Sovereign trials and civilian bodies on frozen roads and the small tight quaver in the voice of everyone he had called from the sedan simply, for a moment, run off him.
The water was very hot. The steam rose slowly around him and gathered against the frameless glass.
He stood under it for a long minute without moving.
Somewhere, halfway through, an unwelcome thought surfaced.

Camilla had, at one point right before he gave her that mission to destroy all toys, casually mentioned observing the entirety of the military base through her spirit sense, as if she were flipping through the pages of a large-format book.
She had catalogued the location of the scientific outpost. Without breaking eye contact with him, she had once described the layout of a coastal town three hundred kilometers away.
A woman capable of that was capable, if she chose, of observing a bathroom through a wall.
Stan considered this, briefly, under the hot water.
Then he shrugged.

Camilla Dragomir was, whatever else she was, a stiff-spined Royal Blood with several years of ingrained aristocratic decorum layered under the Old-World predator instincts. The version of her that had beheaded Elder Fang and destroyed a military base’s equipment was real.
So was the version of her that had inclined her head with the small precise dignity of a woman who considered "not being caught looking" to be one of the fundamental disciplines of adulthood.
She would not. He was reasonably sure she would not. But if she did there was nothing he could do about it.
He turned his face up into the water and stopped thinking about it.
He came out of the bathroom fifteen minutes later in loose dark drawstring trousers and no shirt, running a towel through his hair, the steam rolling out around him in a slow warm exhale.
Camilla was standing at the glass. She turned her head when he entered.

Her red eyes went, very briefly, to the line of his shoulders. To the clean sharp line of his chest. To the small tightness of his stomach. To the small dark strand of wet hair that had fallen across his forehead and had not yet been pushed back.
Her expression did not change. Her eyes were, however, definitely there for one full beat longer than she had intended.
Then she looked, very deliberately, back at the sea.

"Bathroom’s yours whenever you want it," Stan said, matter-of-fact, still working the towel through his hair. "Second door on the left down that hall. Everything works the way it looks like it works. Towels in the cabinet under the sink. If anything confuses you, ask."
"...Thank you, human."
She continued to look at the view from the balcony.
He hung the towel around his neck and turned to survey the bedroom.
He stopped.

Because in the middle of his bedroom, his bedroom, which he had left entering the bathroom featuring one large low bed and one accent chair and precisely no cultivator artifacts, there was now, hovering approximately three feet above the floor, a bed.
Sort of.

It was a broad rectangular slab of pale green stone, roughly the dimensions of a very generous double bed, its surface polished to a soft satiny sheen and its edges carved in the small clean geometric patterns that Stan had, by now, begun to associate with the Void Sovereign’s aesthetic.
It floated, silent and level, in the middle of the room. It cast no shadow. The air beneath it was, when Stan reflexively passed a hand through the space, entirely undisturbed.
He stared at it with a bit of surprise.

Behind him, Camilla, who had followed him into the bedroom with the quiet trailing curiosity of a woman who had decided her tour was starting now whether Stan had officially announced it or not, glanced at the platform, glanced at his face, and produced a small quiet smirk.
"You look surprised, cultivator."
"Well I’m surprised..." Stan looked at her. Obviously Camilla must’ve placed it there while he was bathing.
Her red eyes were bright with the small private amusement of a woman who had, at some point in the past ten minutes, done something and was now enjoying herself.
"What sort of bed is that, a levitating bed, you Cultivators have interesting stuffs of your own..."
"Hmmph~" Camilla smiled slightly.
Seeing her enjoy the praise a bit, Stan’s lip raised as he added, "In the end it’s just stone..."
Camilla felt as though she had been slapped on the face upon hearing that.

"That’s where you’re wrong," saying that she stepped past him toward the platform. She ran one long pale finger along the polished edge. The stone hummed, faintly, at the contact, a low steady note somewhere at the edge of the audible.
"While it looks like stone, it’s very soft and comfortable, not only that it has the effect of calming the mind..." She glanced at him and continued.

"It’s not your normal jade," she said, without turning around. "Grown, not carved. Aligned to the flow of vital Qi. Cool in summer, warm in winter. Provides passive circulation of Qi to the occupant while they rest. In my family it was considered the minimum acceptable furnishing for a Royal Blood in transit."
"Uh-huh."
"I have used it for a very long time."
"Uh-huh."
Stan nodded solemnly as though he were listening to a priceless lecture on ancient cultivator treasures while mentally concluding that it was, nevertheless, still a floating rock.
She turned to face him. The small smirk was still there as she signaled at his bed that was right beside her jade bed.
"Well you didn’t think I’ll have a bed with me right? Did you assume, cultivator, that we are going to share that?"
Stan raised both eyebrows. He considered several possible responses. He selected the most honest one.
"It’s not that unusual for comrades to share a bed."
Camilla’s eyes widened, unable to tell if this was one of his jokes or if he was going at it.
"That is the word you are going with." She asked calmly.
"Yes." Stan smiled, barely holding his laughter in.
Her red eyes glittered, finally concluding he was joking from that laugh. "You are shameless, human."
"I’ve been told."

chapters.title: Chapter 373: Incoming Wave
paragraphs: "You are shameless, human."
"I’ve been told."
Camilla let out a small, quiet, genuinely amused breath, the first fully unguarded laugh he had heard from her since the polar wind.

"For the record," Stan added, gesturing at the wide low sofa in the corner of the bedroom, "there’s a perfectly usable couch right there. I’ll take it. You keep the, the floating jade slab. I don’t want to accidentally drain it of qi or break some ancestral heirloom by rolling over funny."
Camilla considered him. Then, in the small unhurried tone of a woman offering an entirely reasonable observation:
"It is large enough for two, cultivator. Comfortably. The jade will not object. Neither will I."
Seeing her hold his gaze, Stan knew at once that she was trying to get back at him. He wasn’t going to fall for it. He could already imagine what would happen afterward.
He shook his head, "I’ll pass..."
Camilla gritted her teeth, seeing her didn’t fall for her trap, she had a good joke that’ll really hit Stan hard, had he fell for it...
"Whatever I am not, in general, in the habit of sharing a resting place with mortals. Consider it a courtesy extended in light of our comradeship."
Stan looked at the platform. He looked at Camilla. He looked at the couch.
’You’re still playing at that huh?’

He considered, briefly, the small logistical question of what it was going to look like to wake up in his own penthouse next to a Royal Blood vampire the morning after having sworn to five different women, over five separate phone calls, that he had come home to shower and sleep.

He decided, on balance, that the version of this evening in which he refuses that ’offer’ was the version his future self was going to thank him for. The offer hadn’t made much sense to begin with. The fact that Camilla hadn’t immediately withdrawn it after he refused only made him more suspicious.
"My bed is still good and comfortable..."

"How unfortunate. It is your loss, then." Camilla sighed, even though her heart was a bit bitter that Stan didn’t fall to the trap that’ll allow her to use her own joke on him, he wasn’t the only one who should be allowed to joke around like that.
"Very well. As you like." Her eyes glittered again. "But if you change your mind in the night, the jade is patient.
"Noted."
"And I do not snore."
"Also noted."

She inclined her head in mock gravity and stepped past him toward the hallway, apparently in search of the bathroom whose steady, endless flow of water had, some minutes earlier, so nearly undone her composure.
Stan watched her go.
He looked at the floating slab of jade in the middle of his bedroom.
He looked at the couch.
He rubbed a hand slowly down his face.

Then, quietly, to himself, in the small tired amused tone of a man who had returned from Antarctica in one piece and was, apparently, going to sleep on his own bed while a Royal Blood vampire settled into a levitating heirloom in his master bedroom:
’I really do want to crack her, but even with high favourability she’s still a hard nut to crack...’
He kept the towel before settling on his bed...
Meanwhile, Camilla turned toward the bathroom.

She had been thinking, for some minutes now, about the sound. About the mechanism behind the wall. About the small satisfying prospect of stepping into the space, closing the door behind her, and permitting herself the private, uninterrupted study of whatever small clever artifact these New Age humans had built to move water on demand.

She did not, strictly speaking, need to bathe. A vampire of her lineage could remove dust and impurity from her body with a single passing exhalation of Qi, a small automatic maintenance that most Royal Bloods did once or twice a day without conscious thought, in the same way a human might straighten a sleeve.
But she had heard the sound, and she was curious, and curiosity, in her admittedly considered opinion, was one of the few pleasures that survived a long life intact.
She reached the doorway and her hand touched the frame, but then a voice came from the other side of the bedroom...
"Camilla."
She paused to Stan’s voice and turned her head.

Stan was still on bed where she had left him, the towel over the back cushion, his hair still damp at the ends, one hand resting lightly on his knee. He was not looking at her. He was looking, somewhere past her, at the middle distance.
His expression had changed. The small tired ease that had settled into him under the shower had, in the last minute, been replaced by something quieter and more careful.
"How long," he said, "do you think it will take for the Qi to spread out from that frozen region, from the Frost region, as you called it, across the rest of the Earth."
Camilla’s hand dropped from the doorframe.
She stepped, slowly, back into the room. She considered the question.

"I do not know precisely how large this Earth is," she said, after a moment. "The maps I was taught from are, I imagine, no longer accurate. But Qi travels quickly, cultivator. Once a source has begun to release, it does not creep. It spreads." A small pause. "Tens of thousands of kilometers in a single day is not an unusual figure."
Stan’s eyes closed for a moment.
He drew a slow, deep breath. He held it then let it out.
Camilla watched him, the small, precise attention of a woman who had been, over the past several hours, quietly cataloguing the small tells of a man she did not yet fully understand.
He opened his eyes.
"And when it reaches inhabited land," he said, quietly. "What does it do."
Camilla did not answer immediately.
She considered how to phrase it.
Then she said, gently, and it was, he thought, the gentlest tone he had yet heard her use:

"Beasts will change first. The larger and older ones especially. Any creature carrying even a distant trace of beast-kin bloodline will begin to mutate. Slowly at first. Then quickly. The polar bear you killed at the pool, the one whose head you removed with a single strike, that beast had been in Qi-saturated air for perhaps two days. No more. Its strength was already twice that of an unmutated cousin of the same size."

He decided, on balance, that the version of this evening in which he refuses that ’offer’ was the version his future self was going to thank him for.
The offer hadn’t made much sense to begin with.
The fact that Camilla hadn’t immediately withdrawn it after he refused only made him more suspicious.
"My bed is still good and comfortable..."
"How unfortunate.

It is your loss, then." Camilla sighed, even though her heart was a bit bitter that Stan didn’t fall to the trap that’ll allow her to use her own joke on him, he wasn’t the only one who should be allowed to joke around like that.
"Very well.
As you like." Her eyes glittered again.
"But if you change your mind in the night, the jade is patient.
"Noted."
"And I do not snore."
"Also noted."

She inclined her head in mock gravity and stepped past him toward the hallway, apparently in search of the bathroom whose steady, endless flow of water had, some minutes earlier, so nearly undone her composure.
Stan watched her go.
He looked at the floating slab of jade in the middle of his bedroom.
He looked at the couch.
He rubbed a hand slowly down his face.

Then, quietly, to himself, in the small tired amused tone of a man who had returned from Antarctica in one piece and was, apparently, going to sleep on his own bed while a Royal Blood vampire settled into a levitating heirloom in his master bedroom:
’I really do want to crack her, but even with high favourability she’s still a hard nut to crack...’
He kept the towel before settling on his bed...
Meanwhile, Camilla turned toward the bathroom.
She had been thinking, for some minutes now, about the sound.
About the mechanism behind the wall.

About the small satisfying prospect of stepping into the space, closing the door behind her, and permitting herself the private, uninterrupted study of whatever small clever artifact these New Age humans had built to move water on demand.
She did not, strictly speaking, need to bathe.

A vampire of her lineage could remove dust and impurity from her body with a single passing exhalation of Qi, a small automatic maintenance that most Royal Bloods did once or twice a day without conscious thought, in the same way a human might straighten a sleeve.
But she had heard the sound, and she was curious, and curiosity, in her admittedly considered opinion, was one of the few pleasures that survived a long life intact.
She reached the doorway and her hand touched the frame, but then a voice came from the other side of the bedroom...
"Camilla."
She paused to Stan’s voice and turned her head.
Stan was still on bed where she had left him, the towel over the back cushion, his hair still damp at the ends, one hand resting lightly on his knee.
He was not looking at her.
He was looking, somewhere past her, at the middle distance.
His expression had changed.
The small tired ease that had settled into him under the shower had, in the last minute, been replaced by something quieter and more careful.
"How long," he said, "do you think it will take for the Qi to spread out from that frozen region, from the Frost region, as you called it, across the rest of the Earth."
Camilla’s hand dropped from the doorframe.
She stepped, slowly, back into the room.
She considered the question.
"I do not know precisely how large this Earth is," she said, after a moment.
"The maps I was taught from are, I imagine, no longer accurate.
But Qi travels quickly, cultivator.
Once a source has begun to release, it does not creep.
It spreads." A small pause.
"Tens of thousands of kilometers in a single day is not an unusual figure."
Stan’s eyes closed for a moment.
He drew a slow, deep breath.
He held it then let it out.
Camilla watched him, the small, precise attention of a woman who had been, over the past several hours, quietly cataloguing the small tells of a man she did not yet fully understand.
He opened his eyes.
"And when it reaches inhabited land," he said, quietly.
"What does it do."
Camilla did not answer immediately.
She considered how to phrase it.
Then she said, gently, and it was, he thought, the gentlest tone he had yet heard her use:
"Beasts will change first.
The larger and older ones especially.
Any creature carrying even a distant trace of beast-kin bloodline will begin to mutate.
Slowly at first.
Then quickly.
The polar bear you killed at the pool, the one whose head you removed with a single strike, that beast had been in Qi-saturated air for perhaps two days.
No more.
Its strength was already twice that of an unmutated cousin of the same size."

chapters.title: Chapter 374: The Other Path
paragraphs: "Beasts will change first. The larger and older ones especially. Any creature carrying even a distant trace of beast-kin bloodline will begin to mutate. Slowly at first. Then quickly. The polar bear you killed at the pool, the one whose head you removed with a single strike, that beast had been in Qi-saturated air for perhaps two days. No more. Its strength was already twice that of an unmutated cousin of the same size."
Stan was very still. "Two days, huh?"
"Yes. Two days."
"Thats crazy."

"I suppose it is, from your perspective. That was merely the edge of the saturation, where the density of Qi was still thin. Closer to the source, or after longer exposure, the change is greater. And there are stronger bloodlines than a polar bear's. Wolves. Great cats. Corvids. Cetaceans." A small pause. "The oceans will be... interesting."
Stan let out a long, slow breath.
"And humans?"
Camilla was quiet for a moment.

"Some," she said. "Not all. Perhaps not even most. Any human line carrying even a fragmented inheritance of an old bloodline, beast-kin, demihuman, True Human, cultivator ancestry that never fully faded, will begin to stir. Slowly. It will not look like power at first. It will look like, restlessness. Vivid dreams. Sudden strength in a moment of fear. Small children speaking to animals that speak back."
She lifted one shoulder, a small elegant fraction of a shrug.
"Later, it will look like power."
Stan sat very still.
The sea, outside the tall glass, had gone from gold to something deeper.
"Thank you," he said, quietly. "For telling me."
Camilla studied him for a moment.
Then, very quietly: "You are welcome, cultivator."
She turned back toward the bathroom.
At the threshold, she paused once more, one hand on the doorframe, her back to him, and permitted herself one small final glance over her shoulder.
Stan remained where he was, his attention fixed somewhere beyond the windows.
Camilla filed that expression away, quietly, in the small careful place where she was, day by day, building her private inventory of the man she had bound herself to.
She stepped into the bathroom.
She closed the door behind her. Taking a deep breath, she stood, for a moment, simply looking at the room.

It was strange, in ways she was going to need to sit with. Everything was polished porcelain, chrome, and pale stone. No spirit formations along the walls. No arrays carved into the corners. No engraved runes catching light. And yet every object appeared, on closer inspection, to have been deliberately placed, arranged with the careful precision of someone who had designed the space with purpose and paid, presumably, an enormous sum to bring it into existence.
Her attention settled on the shower. At first glance, it resembled nothing more than a length of chrome jutting out from a stone wall. Nothing more. No Qi. No spirit stones. No inscriptions. Nothing.
She extended her spiritual sense into it. 'Solid metal with hollow channels running back through the wall... Huh?'
'They're also small moving components housed inside a valve at the base. Ingenious and entirely mundane. Impressive...'

Her crimson eyes settled upon the small handle beneath the fixture. Her spiritual sense flowed through the metal, revealing the intricate arrangement hidden behind the wall. Pipes. Valves. Rotating seals. Each component moved in precise relation to the others. It was an activation mechanism. Crude by the standards of ancient artifact engineering, yet undeniably ingenious in its own way, accomplishing its purpose without the aid of qi or formations.
She reached out and turned the handle slightly.
Nothing came out, but knowing that would happen, She adjusted it, a careful, considered fraction further,

And a stream of icy water poured out of the fixture above her head, cascaded over her hair and shoulders, and down her skin with the small unhurried thoroughness of a system operating exactly as designed.
Camilla did not flinch nor did she step back.
She did not, in any sense that a mortal observer could have identified, react at all.

She simply stood there, perfectly composed, as the icy water ran down over her, and permitted her spiritual sense to follow the flow backward through the pipes into the wall and along a length of channel and up, up, up through the building to some larger reservoir she chose not to trace further.
"...Interesting," she said, quietly, to the empty bathroom.
She reached for the handle again. A measured, careful turn. The water gradually warmed.

Not through spiritual fire. Not through a heating array. Not through any conceivable manipulation of Qi. Simply, through the small clever adjustment of a mechanism she could feel operating deep within the wall.
Her crimson eyes lingered on the fixture with the small focused attention of a Royal Blood who was, quietly, revising a great many assumptions.
She experimented.

One motion adjusted the temperature. Another changed the pressure. A third, hidden along the side of the fixture, redirected the flow entirely from the overhead into a second unit on a sliding rail she had not initially noticed. Each function was precise. Each was reliable. Each was, as far as she could tell, having now traced the entire mechanism from the wall to the building to the reservoir, entirely, unambiguously, gloriously mundane.
No cultivator, at any time in the long history of the Old Era, would have devoted this much thought to the comfort of an ordinary mortal.
And yet, humanity had.

In the several thousand years since Qi had left the world, ordinary humans had not curled up and died. They had not, in some diminished and pitiful form, simply hung on. They had built this. They had chosen a road that was not the road of cultivation, and they had walked it very far.
Not a road of Qi.
A road of knowledge.

For the first time since she had woken beneath the ice, Camilla permitted herself the small quiet acknowledgement that the descendants of the ancient mortals were, in their own strange and specific way, brilliant.
She lifted her chin under the warm water and allowed herself, finally, to bathe.

chapters.title: Chapter 375: Keep Your Secrets
paragraphs: She had just finished bathing when she felt it. Her movements came to an immediate halt.
Her crimson eyes narrowed ever so slightly.
"...Impossible."
She had felt it clearly. She had not imagined it. It brushed against the edge of her spiritual sense with the unmistakable resonance of the thing itself.
'Qi.'
Fresh qi. Pure. Concentrated. Being deliberately drawn into a cultivator's body before circulating through their meridians.
Someone was cultivating. Somewhere nearby. Within this very apartment
For the briefest moment, Camilla stood perfectly still, extending her spiritual sense once more to confirm what she had perceived.
The result remained unchanged. Without haste, she lifted a hand.

A thin veil of crimson spiritual essence rippled over her skin, carrying away every remaining droplet of water before dissipating into nothingness. Her hair dried in the same quiet motion, each strand settling neatly into place as though untouched by moisture.

Only then did she dress. She smoothed the faintest crease from her robes, adjusted the fall of her hair over one shoulder, and allowed her expression to return to its customary calm, betraying none of the surprise stirring beneath.
Then she opened the bathroom door.
Her steps were as measured and graceful as ever as she made her way back toward the bedroom.
Stan sat cross-legged on the low, wide sofa in the corner.
Eyes closed. Hands resting palm-up on his knees. Back straight. Breathing slow.
The floating slab of pale green jade hovered nearby, silent and level. Camilla registered it in her peripheral attention and dismissed it. It was not the source of what she was feeling.

It was Stan. Around him, invisible to any ordinary human eye, and unmistakable to hers, thin ambient streams of Qi were gathering. Curling in from the air. Drifting inward from the corners of the room. Being drawn along the length of his spine and cycled, slow and clean, through the small precise architecture of a meridian system she had already noted was cleaner than any modern human's had any right to be.
His aura was rising.
Steadily. Cleanly. With the small controlled competence of a cultivator who had, at some point, learned exactly what he was doing.
Camilla's pupils contracted.

This was not possible. This city contained no Qi. She had confirmed it herself, in the hour after they had arrived, one small pulse of her spirit sense across Inksea, one careful scan of the ambient atmospheric density, one honest and unsentimental conclusion that the island was, in cultivation terms, a wasteland. There's no Qi at all...
And yet Stan's cultivation was progressing as though he were seated inside a first-class ancestral cultivation ground.

She watched. Then his aura surged. The pressure in the room briefly intensified, a small clean pulse of Qi settling into place in some newly stabilized layer of his cultivation base, and then smoothed out again, level and quiet, as if a small internal foundation had just been laid and had already dried.
A breakthrough. A clean one.
Camilla did not move.
She watched as Stan let out a slow, controlled exhale and opened his eyes.
His gaze found her immediately. "...What?"

He asked it casually. In the small unhurried tone of a man who had been meditating in his own bedroom and had opened his eyes to find his houseguest staring at him and could see nothing particularly unusual about it.
Camilla did not answer immediately.
She walked, slowly, several steps closer to the sofa. Her red eyes stayed on him.
"How," she said, "are you cultivating."
"Ah." Stan tilted his head. "That."
"There is no Qi in this city, human. Yet your cultivation base just advanced."
"It did. Just a minor stage."
"You're yet to answer how."
Stan smiled, the small, unhurried, genuinely amused smile of a man who had no intention whatsoever of answering the question. "...Trade secret."
Camilla's eyes narrowed.
Inside his own head, Stan permitted himself a very small internal chuckle.

The truth, in fact, was mildly ridiculous. He had opened the System's inventory in the private back of his mind and released a small measured trickle of the Spirit Pool Qi he had brought back from Antarctica, the same Qi Camilla had traded him, eight times rebated, directly into his own dantian. From the outside, to any observer with a spirit sense, it looked like a man drawing Qi from the ambient air of a city that did not have any.
It was, in his considered opinion, one of the great small advantages of his particular situation.
And one he had no intention of ever explaining to anyone. So he simply smiled and said nothing.
Camilla studied him for a long moment. Indirect probing was, apparently, not going to work.
'Fine.' She decided, in that moment, to ask the question she had been quietly holding since Antarctica.
"When," she said calmly, "are you going to admit to your true cultivation realm."
Stan raised an eyebrow.

"I refuse to believe," she continued, in the same measured tone, "that a cultivator in possession of the volume of spirit Qi you produced in that cave, capable of casually restoring himself from mortal injury with an artifact pill, and now cultivating in a city with no ambient Qi as if he were seated at the heart of an ancestral formation, is a Qi Refining stage practitioner."
She held his gaze. "You are concealing your true realm."
She said it with the small, absolute certainty of a woman who had been quietly assembling this conclusion for hours and was now presenting it, fully formed, and expected acknowledgement.

Stan almost laughed. Because the thing was, the actual thing was, his cultivation realm was, in fact, exactly what she was seeing. Genesis Realm initial stage. No hidden ninth heaven. No concealed transcendent tier. No shrouded eleven-thousand-year-old ancestor lurking behind the pleasant twenty-something face.
The absurd Qi reserve came from the inventory. The impossible cultivation speed came from the System.
The unaccountable resources came from a rebate multiplier applied to money he had spent on beautiful women.
The combat feats came from installed mastery he had paid points for.
None of it was hidden depth. All of it was hidden machinery.

But if a Royal Blood vampire, with all the small ingrained assumptions of Old Era hierarchy behind her red eyes, wanted to conclude that he was a concealed high cultivator disguising himself as an ordinary young man for reasons of his own,
Then that misunderstanding was going to work entirely in his favor.
For as long as he could sustain it.
Which, based on the past several minutes, was going to be quite a while.
He smiled and said nothing.
Camilla watched him.
The silence stretched. Then, slowly, the small corner of her mouth curved.
"...So," she said, softly. "You refuse to admit it."
Stan spread his hands, palms up, in the small universal gesture of a man declining to comment.
"Very well." A small elegant tilt of her head. "Keep your secrets, human. I will not press. One day, your true realm will reveal itself, whether you intend it to or not."

chapters.title: Chapter 376: An Evening Stroll
paragraphs: "Very well." She tilted her head slightly. "Keep your secrets, human. I will not press. One day, your true realm will reveal itself, whether you intend it to or not."

She turned to go. At the doorway she paused, one hand on the frame, and glanced back over her shoulder. Her red eyes glittered with the small private satisfaction of a woman who had, in her own private assessment, finally caught him.
"I knew it," she said, quietly, almost to herself.
Then she stepped out into the hallway.
Stan watched her go. He waited until the small sound of her footsteps had receded down the hall.
’...She’s completely convinced.’ He let out a slow breath. ’Perfect.’
He tipped his head back against the bed, closed his eyes, and let the small warm quiet of his own apartment settle over him for the first time in what felt like an eternity.
Outside the glass, the sea had gone from gold to a deep soft blue.
The city lights, along the coast below, were beginning to come on.
Meanwhile, Camilla found her coat where she had draped it over the arm of the sofa in the living room.
She lifted it. Shook out the small creases. Drew it around her shoulders with the fluid, unhurried grace she brought to every physical motion. Then she started, in unhurried fashion, toward the door.
Stan looked up from the sofa.
"Where are you going."
"Out."
"Out?"
"Out, human. Into the city. To walk."

Stan uncrossed his legs and rose in one smooth motion. His hand lifted slightly, the small automatic gesture of a man about to raise a reasonable objection about a Royal Blood vampire wandering unsupervised through a modern coastal city at nightfall.
Camilla stopped at the threshold.

She turned her head. She looked at his half-raised hand. She looked at his face. Then she smiled, the small elegant private smile of a woman who had, for the entire afternoon, been waiting for exactly this expression.
"What," she said, softly. "You are not confident in your blood contract?"
Stan’s hand froze midair.

He was, in fact, entirely confident in the blood contract. It was airtight. She could not act against him. She could not lie to him. She could not, by any Old Era rule that had ever governed a Royal Blood’s binding, betray the terms of what they had sworn to one another on the ice.
He was also, in general, of the disposition that rather safe than sorry was a life philosophy that had kept him breathing this long and did not need revising this afternoon.
But she was not wrong.
And there was, he recognized with a small tired resignation, no productive way to make her be wrong out loud.
He lowered his hand.
He waved her off. "Enjoy the walk."
"I intend to." She inclined her head in mock gravity, produced a small satisfied scoff at the corner of her mouth, and stepped through the door.
It closed softly behind her.
Stan stood in the middle of the living room for a long moment, looking at the door.
Then he sighed, sat back down on the sofa, folded his legs beneath him, and resumed his meditation.
Inksea in the early evening was, Camilla decided within the first three blocks, a strange city.

Not strange in the way a foreign kingdom in her own era might have been strange, with its own tongue and its own customs. But strange in a deeper way. Strange in the way that the entire substrate of ordinary life had, over several thousand years, drifted into shapes she had no vocabulary for.

The pavement was smooth and even, laid in the small clean geometric patterns of a place designed by people who cared what pavement looked like. The lights above the streets came on at their own schedule, without any lantern-lighter passing to touch them. The vehicles that moved along the roads made no sound of hoof against stone, only the soft continuous hum of the small clever mechanisms she had been quietly cataloguing since the sedan ride.
She walked.
She did not, in her own honest self-assessment, know where she was walking. She did not care. The point of the walk was not the destination. The point of the walk was the walking.
She let her red eyes move across everything.

The advertising screens on the sides of the taller buildings, cycling their patient loops of colour and text. The small groups of young people moving in and out of the small warm-lit shops along the main avenue, laughing at something one of them had said. The old man walking a small ridiculous dog on a leash. The couple sharing a paper cup of some frozen dessert. The woman in professional dress standing at a corner speaking into a small handheld device with the small controlled irritation of a person who had already explained something twice.
None of them, at first glance, appeared to notice her.
That, in itself, was interesting.
Not because they were incapable of sensing her.
But because she had given them almost nothing to sense.

Her aura was folded so tightly against herself that it scarcely extended beyond her own skin, every instinctive pressure of a Royal Blood deliberately retracted. Had she allowed even a fraction of it to leak into the air, this street would have changed within moments. Conversations would have faltered. Children would have gone quiet. Dogs would have tucked their tails. Every ordinary mortal within reach would have felt the inexplicable certainty that something ancient and dangerous had entered their world.
Instead, they saw only a woman.
Or rather, they believed they did.

She watched, with the small unhurried attention of a scientist, as one young man walking toward her on the pavement raised his eyes to her face in the ordinary passing way of a stranger, held her gaze for exactly half a second, and then flinched.

It was subtle. He did not stop walking. He did not make a sound. He simply flinched, some small deep part of his lizard brain registering the presence of a predator his conscious mind had never been taught to recognize, and looked away, continuing on with his evening at a very slightly accelerated pace.
Camilla catalogued the flinch.
She continued walking.

A woman coming out of one of the small warm-lit shops looked up as she passed, and paused, one hand still on the door handle, the small unfocused smile of a person who had been thinking about something else fading from her face. Her eyes settled on Camilla’s for one held moment. Camilla let her look. The woman’s small unfocused smile did not return. She stepped back inside the shop.
Interesting.

At the corner two blocks further down, a small handful of teenagers standing around a low stone bench went visibly quiet as she walked past. One of them, a girl of perhaps sixteen, with the small bright fashion sense of a young person who had put visible thought into her outfit that morning, muttered something to her friends after Camilla had passed that Camilla, with her spirit sense idling at low sensitivity, chose not to hear.
Something about her eyes, she suspected.

The eyes were, she was slowly beginning to understand, the one thing no amount of carefully restrained presence could entirely conceal. Her clothes were, by modern standards, somewhat old-fashioned, a small dark high-collared thing Stan had allowed her to wear from his own closet with a scarf borrowed from the coat rack over one shoulder, but not so out of place on the streets of a stylish coastal city that anyone would look twice.
But the eyes.

The eyes were a very specific shade of red, and no modern human on Earth had that shade as a natural eye colour. Even with her aura hidden, every ordinary mortal she passed lingered on them for a heartbeat too long, their instincts whispering that something was not quite right before reason dismissed the feeling and carried them onward.
She was, she decided, going to find it more entertaining than annoying.

chapters.title: Chapter 377: Among Mortals
paragraphs: Somewhere along the promenade, a small ridiculous incident happened.
A ball rolled to a stop against the toe of her boot.
Camilla looked down at it

It was a small brightly coloured sphere of the kind she had, in the past several hours, seen small human children kick around in every public space they had passed. Made of the same soft synthetic material as most modern objects. She had, she realized, no specific opinion about it.

A small human, perhaps five years old, perhaps six, with the earnest determined expression of a child who had chased a ball across a public space and was now committing fully to the recovery mission, arrived at her feet in a small breathless rush.
He stopped.
He looked at the ball.
He looked at her boot.
He looked, slowly, up at her face.
Camilla looked down at him.
There was a small held moment.

She had, in years, been looked at with fear by mortals of every station in every land she had walked through. She had learned to distinguish the small shades of it, the sharp bright fear of a soldier facing his death, the slow quiet fear of a courtier who understood exactly what she was, the small useful animal fear of a servant who would say nothing later. She had learned to use fear.
The small human at her feet was not afraid.
He was, in fact, examining her with the same open, unfiltered, entirely undiplomatic curiosity that Camilla imagined he brought to every new adult who had entered his field of vision that day.
"Auntie," he said.
Camilla blinked.
"Auntie," he said again, this time with the small patient repetition of a child who was not sure the tall lady had heard him the first time. "Have your eyes been red since you were born?"
Camilla stood very still.
Somewhere in the middle distance, a mother-shaped adult was calling a name that was presumably his and was not yet close enough to intervene.
Camilla considered the question.

It was, by any measure, a monumentally stupid question. It was the kind of question that only a small human could have asked, in the specific window of human development where one had learned that eyes came in colours but had not yet learned that certain colours warranted certain small silences. It was, in fact, so stupid that it circled all the way back around to being, in its own small unpolished way, sincere.
She crouched, in a single fluid motion, until her eyes were level with his.
He did not step back.
"Yes," she said, gravely. "Since I was born."
"Oh." He considered this with the small serious face of a child processing new information. "Cool."
He bent down. He picked up his ball. He looked back up at her.
"Thank you," he said, in the small careful voice of a child who had remembered his manners at the last possible second.

Then he turned and ran back across the promenade toward the mother-shaped adult, who scooped him up with the small anxious relief of a parent who had briefly, three seconds ago, considered the possibility of a missing child and was now processing having merely a returned one.
Camilla straightened.
She watched the mother carry the child away.

The mother, at some point during the carrying, glanced back over her shoulder at Camilla, and, upon meeting her eyes, produced the small polite alarmed smile of a woman who did not want to look like she was hurrying and was, in fact, hurrying.
Camilla inclined her head, one small precise fraction of a degree.
The mother turned around and walked, at a slightly increased pace, in the opposite direction.
Camilla stood on the promenade for a moment longer.
Then, quietly, entirely to herself, in the small amused tone of a woman who had not expected the evening to produce this particular small piece of information:
"...Cool...huh"
She continued walking.
She did not, in her own honest self-assessment, keep track of the time.

The sun set. The coastal light softened from gold into blue and from blue into the deeper indigo of a coastal evening. The advertising screens on the taller buildings grew brighter against the darkening sky. The lights along the promenade came fully on. The small warm-lit shops began, one by one, to lower their shutters and close for the night. The last of the day’s small crowds thinned into the smaller quieter crowds of a coastal city’s evening, young couples walking arm-in-arm, older people out for their nightly turn along the sea, the occasional lone figure moving with the small purposeful stride of a person going home.
Camilla walked past all of them.
She was, quietly, being surprised by how much she was enjoying herself.

The Inksea night was cool without being cold. The sea breeze off the coast was gentle. The small clean geometric patterns of the pavement, laid out beneath streetlights that came on at their own schedule and hummed at frequencies she could hear if she listened, were pleasant to walk on. The city did not, at any point in her walk, threaten her. It did not, at any point in her walk, particularly notice her. It simply, was. Continued. Rolled forward around her in its small patient hundreds of unremarkable evenings.
She catalogued it, all of it, with the quiet unhurried absorption of a woman who was, very slowly, deciding that she was going to enjoy the New Age.

Eventually, when the promenade had emptied to the small handful of late walkers and the small warm-lit shops had all closed and the moon had risen far enough that the sea beneath it had gone into the deep silvered black of full night, Camilla turned, at last, and made her unhurried way back toward Aurelia Heights.
She got into the elevator, and not long after it began to rise in silence.

The doors opened onto the small private vestibule of Stan’s floor. Camilla stepped out. She tapped her hand against the reader in the small precise imitation of the gesture she had watched Stan perform multiple times that afternoon.
The door unlocked with a soft mechanical click.
She stepped inside. The penthouse was dim.

Not dark, the tall glass along the far wall admitted the soft silver of the moon, and the small ambient lights along the low edges of the walls glowed at their patient nighttime setting, and the city lights along the coast below cast a soft warm underglow across the ceiling.
But quiet.
Stan was on the sofa.

Cross-legged. Eyes closed. Hands resting palm-up on his knees. The small clean line of his shoulders steady with the slow controlled rhythm of a cultivator deep in his practice. Around him, faint and invisible to any ordinary observer, the ambient Qi of the room drifted inward in slow patient streams, pulled, apparently, out of a city that contained no Qi at all, and settled into the small precise architecture of his meridians with the small unhurried competence of a cultivator seated at the heart of an ancestral formation.
Camilla stopped, one foot inside the door.
She looked at him.
Her red eyes narrowed by exactly one shade.

Then, slowly, the small corner of her mouth curved into the private amused expression of a woman who had already, that afternoon, filed her private conclusion about this and was quietly enjoying the additional confirmation.
She scoffed, softly, to herself.

"...Hidden master," she murmured, in the small amused tone of a woman speaking to no one in particular. "Cultivating in a Qi-empty city as though he were seated at a sect ancestor’s grave. Genesis Realm, he says. Genesis Realm."
She shook her head.

She stepped out of her boots. She hung the coat on the rack by the door. She padded quietly across the pale wood floor toward the bedroom, catching one final glance back at Stan, still cross-legged, still perfectly composed, entirely unbothered by her return, before slipping through the doorway.
The floating slab of pale green jade waited exactly where she had left it, hovering silent and level at its patient distance above the floor.
She approached it.
She ran one long pale finger along the polished edge. The stone hummed, faintly, at the contact, the small quiet note of a resonance she had known since childhood.
She let out a small unhurried breath.

Then she stepped onto the jade and lay back along its cool satiny length, arranging her hair over one shoulder in a single fluid motion, folding her hands on her stomach, and closing her eyes with the small satisfied composure of a Royal Blood settling in for the night.
For a long moment, she simply lay there.

The soft continuous ambient hum of the city drifted in through the tall glass. The distant small sound of the sea moved beneath it. The faint, invisible circulation of Qi in the next room continued at its patient rhythm.
Camilla’s mouth curved, very slightly, one final time.

’Cool,’ she thought, remembering the small human on the promenade with his small ridiculous question and his small serious face, and, still smiling, drifted into the deep unhurried rest of a Royal Blood at the end of a long strange first day in the New Age.

chapters.title: Chapter 378: Come on in...
paragraphs: Around an hour slipped by in heavy silence.

Then Camilla stirred. She activated her hovering jade bed on the far side of the room, its surface glowing with a soft, pearlescent light. Turning toward Stan, her crimson eyes caught the lamplight and seemed to flicker with an inner glow as she spoke, her voice calm and detached.
"I’ve erected a Qi wall around myself, my aura, my presence, everything is completely sealed. They won’t see, sense, or hear me. Whatever you do with them is none of my concern."
Stan glanced over and saw it at once: a transparent, glass-like barrier of shimmering Qi enveloping her bed like a flawless crystalline box, isolating her entirely from the rest of the room.
He frowned. "Who are you talking about?"
Before Camilla could answer, a firm knock echoed through the chamber.
Stan rose from the bed, heart quickening with a mix of curiosity and anticipation. He crossed the room and pulled the door open.

Standing there were Maya and Sophie, both dressed to devastating effect. Their outfits were matching yet distinctively seductive: sleek, backless midnight-black dresses that clung to every curve like a second skin.

The fabric was a luxurious, silky material that shimmered faintly under the light, cut dangerously low in the front to showcase their full, rounded cleavage. Deep plunging necklines framed the soft, inviting swell of their breasts, the inner curves glistening subtly as if kissed by oil.
The dresses hugged their narrow waists before flaring over wide, fertile hips, the hem riding high on their smooth thighs to reveal long, toned legs.
Every breath they took made the fabric stretch taut across their chests, accentuating the deep valley between their breasts and the gentle bounce of their figures.
"Surprise, Stan!" they chimed in unison, bright smiles lighting their faces. Each girl slipped an arm around one of his shoulders, pressing their warm, soft bodies against him.
Maya leaned in first, her full lips parted invitingly. Stan met her with a deep, hungry kiss.

He cupped the back of her neck, tilting her head as his mouth claimed hers, slow at first, then bolder. His tongue traced the seam of her lips before sliding inside, stroking and teasing with deliberate sensuality.

Maya melted into him with a soft moan, her body molding flush against his bare chest, her heavy breasts compressing warmly against his skin. She tasted sweet and faintly of cherries, her tongue dancing eagerly with his in wet, heated strokes.

While they kissed, Sophie waited with visible impatience, her fingers tracing slow, sensual circles over Stan’s sculpted chest. Her touch drifted lower, boldly gliding down his abdomen until her palm cupped the growing bulge at his crotch, giving a gentle, teasing squeeze.
"We couldn’t wait," she purred against his ear, voice husky with need. "We couldn’t bear the thought of you sleeping alone tonight... so we decided to come together."

paragraphs: Morning light filtered softly through the curtains. Stan stirred first, the warm weight of Maya and Sophie still pressed against him on either side. For a moment he simply lay there, savoring the soft press of their bare skin, the gentle rise and fall of their breathing. Then his senses stretched outward, quiet, precise.
Camilla was gone. Not in the room. Not elsewhere in the house. Not even lingering somewhere outside within his range. She had not returned at any point during the night.
Stan exhaled slowly through his nose, a quiet sigh. ’How long does she plan to stay like this...’

Before the thought could settle too deeply, Maya shifted against his side. Her lashes fluttered, and a soft, contented sound escaped her as she nuzzled closer, her full breast brushing warm against his ribs.
A moment later Sophie stirred as well, stretching languidly before tucking herself more firmly against him, one leg sliding over his thigh.

Maya’s eyes opened fully. A slow, sleepy smile curved her lips. "Good morning, my love..." Her voice was husky with sleep, warm and intimate. She tilted her face up and pressed a soft, lingering kiss to the corner of his mouth.

Sophie followed almost immediately, her hand drifting across his chest in a lazy caress. "Mmm... morning." She kissed the other side of his jaw, lips soft and warm. "You feel even better to wake up to than you did last night."
Stan’s arms tightened around both of them, drawing them closer. "Morning, both of you." His voice was low, still rough from sleep. "Sleep well?"

Maya hummed against his skin, fingers tracing idle patterns over the hard planes of his chest. "Too well. I almost don’t want to get up." Her thigh shifted higher along his, the soft press of her body openly affectionate. "You make a dangerously good pillow."

Sophie’s soft laugh vibrated against his other side. "He does. Warm... solid... and he doesn’t even try to escape when we cling to him." Her hand slid lower, resting possessively over his stomach. "I could stay like this all morning."

They lingered that way for a while, soft kisses, slow caresses, the easy intimacy of three bodies still tangled together under the sheets. Maya eventually propped herself up on one elbow, looking down at him with a playful, affectionate expression.

"We should probably get up at some point," she said, though she made no move to leave his side. "Especially since..." She glanced toward the kitchen direction with a small, knowing smile. "Someone has absolutely nothing edible left in this house."

Sophie lifted her head, eyes sparkling with quiet amusement. "She’s right. I checked the cabinets last night while looking for the tray. Empty. Completely. You were clearly living on pure willpower and whatever we brought."
Stan gave a low, rueful chuckle. "Caught."

Maya leaned down and brushed another soft kiss across his lips. "Then it’s settled. We’ll go shopping with you. Stock this place properly so our king doesn’t starve between visits." Her fingers traced a slow line down his chest as she spoke, lingering. "And maybe pick up a few things for... later."

Sophie stretched again, the motion making her soft breasts press more firmly against him for a moment. "I like that plan. Breakfast out, shopping together, then back here." She smiled against his shoulder. "Sounds like a perfect morning."
Stan’s hands stroked slowly along their backs, savoring the warm silk of their skin. "Then that’s what we’ll do."
The three of them remained tangled together a little longer, exchanging soft kisses and quiet, affectionate words.

With that they rose from the bed together, still warm from sleep and each other’s skin. A quick shared shower followed, steam rising around them once more as soft hands moved over wet bodies with familiar, affectionate ease.

Maya soaped Stan’s chest while Sophie rinsed his back; his own palms glided over the curves of their hips and the full undersides of their breasts, lingering just long enough to draw soft smiles and quiet, contented sounds. No urgency this time, only the easy intimacy of people who already knew every inch of one another.

They dried off and dressed without hurry. Maya slipped into a soft, form-fitting dress that hugged her waist and flared gently over her hips; Sophie chose a similar style in a complementary shade, the fabric clinging just enough to hint at the full curves beneath.
Stan pulled on dark jeans and a simple black shirt that sat well across his shoulders. The three of them moved around one another with quiet coordination.

In the elevator the close space only heightened the lingering warmth between them. Maya leaned lightly against Stan’s side, her soft breast brushing his arm with every small shift of the descending cabin.

Sophie stood on his other side, her fingers briefly linking with his. The mirrored walls reflected the easy way they stood together, close, comfortable, still carrying the quiet afterglow of the night.
"You smell good," Maya murmured, tilting her face up toward him with a small smile. "Whatever that soap was... I like it on you."
Sophie gave a soft, agreeing hum. "Mm. Makes me want to skip the shopping and drag him straight back upstairs."
Stan’s low chuckle filled the quiet elevator. "Tempting. But if we do that, we’ll be back to empty cabinets by tonight. And I seem to remember two very persuasive women insisting I stock up."
Maya’s fingers traced a brief, playful line along his forearm. "We’re responsible like that. Sometimes."
The elevator doors opened onto the underground garage. Stan led them to his sleek black Audi, unlocking it with a soft click.
Maya settled into the front seat; Sophie claimed the back, immediately leaning forward between the seats so she could stay close.

As the engine purred to life and the car pulled out into the morning light, Maya rested her hand lightly on Stan’s thigh, her thumb stroking slow, absent circles through the denim. Sophie’s fingers found the back of his neck from behind, tracing the short hair there with gentle affection.
"I like seeing you drive," Sophie said softly, her voice warm. "You look so focused... and a little dangerous."
Maya smiled, her hand still resting possessively on his leg. "He always does. It’s unfair, really. We should be the ones distracting him, not the other way around."
Stan glanced briefly at Maya, then checked the mirror to catch Sophie’s reflection, a small, genuine smile tugging at his mouth. "You’re both doing a fairly good job of that already."
The city slid past the windows in soft morning light.

chapters.title: Chapter 390: Trading Hub
paragraphs: The Audi glided smoothly through the morning traffic, the city waking up around them in soft gold light. Maya’s hand remained on Stan’s thigh, her thumb still tracing slow, absent circles through the fabric of his jeans. Sophie leaned forward from the back seat, her chin nearly resting on the headrest between them, fingers lightly brushing the nape of his neck whenever the car took a gentle turn.
Maya glanced at the unfamiliar streets and tilted her head. "So... where exactly are we going? This doesn’t look like any grocery run I’ve ever been on."
Sophie hummed in agreement, her breath warm near his ear. "Yeah. You’ve got that focused ’I know exactly where I’m headed’ look. Spill."

Stan’s mouth curved in a small, easy smile as he changed lanes. "There’s a trading hub not far from here. Prime Stock Trading Hub. Not the kind of place most people think of for everyday shopping, but they carry everything, high-quality produce, specialty cuts, imported goods, household staples. One stop and the house will be properly stocked for a while."
Maya’s fingers gave his thigh a light, appreciative squeeze. "A whole trading hub just to restock your kitchen? You really don’t do anything halfway, do you?"
"Wouldn’t want my two favorite guests going hungry," he answered, voice low and warm. "Or me, for that matter."

Sophie laughed softly, the sound intimate in the quiet cabin of the car. "Listen to him. Acting like we didn’t just spend half the night making sure he was thoroughly taken care of." Her fingertips traced a slow line along the side of his neck. "Though I suppose feeding him is the next responsible step."

Maya leaned a little closer, her soft breast brushing against his arm as she spoke. "Responsible and enjoyable. I like the combination." She glanced out the window, then back at him with a playful glint in her eyes. "Just don’t get too distracted by all the options once we’re inside. I’d rather not lose you to a particularly impressive cut of steak."
Stan chuckled, the sound low in his chest. "I’ll try to restrain myself. But no promises if they have those aged wagyu portions you both like."
"Bribery already?" Sophie teased, her voice rich with amusement. "We’re not even there yet and he’s already planning to spoil us."
"Can you blame me?" he replied, glancing briefly at Maya before checking the mirror to catch Sophie’s reflection. "I have excellent taste in company. It tends to extend to everything else."
Maya’s thumb resumed its slow circles. "Mm. Flattery and fine food. Dangerous combination this early in the morning."
Sophie rested her chin more firmly against the headrest, smiling. "Dangerous in the best way. I’m already curious what else he’s going to try to talk us into once we’re walking those aisles."
"Nothing you won’t enjoy," Stan said, the corner of his mouth lifting. "I promise."
The conversation flowed easily after that, soft, affectionate remarks, quiet laughter, the occasional lingering touch.

Maya’s hand never left his thigh for long; Sophie’s fingers continued their gentle exploration of the short hair at the back of his neck. The enclosed space of the car held the faint, clean scent of the soap they had shared that morning, mixed with the subtle warmth of their nice feminine perfume.

After another few turns through quieter streets, the large modern structure of the Prime Stock Trading Hub came into view, glass and steel rising cleanly against the morning sky, its broad entrance already seeing a steady stream of early shoppers and delivery vehicles.
Stan guided the Audi into the underground parking levels, the engine’s soft purr echoing briefly off the concrete walls as he found a space near the elevators.
He put the car in park and killed the engine. For a moment the three of them simply sat there, the quiet intimacy of the drive still lingering between them.
Maya gave his thigh one last slow stroke before withdrawing her hand with a small, satisfied smile. "Well... shall we go make sure our king’s kitchen is worthy of him again?"
Sophie was already reaching for her door handle, eyes bright. "Lead the way."
Stan stepped out, the cool underground air brushing his skin. Sophie and Maya stepped out as well.
With that they walked together toward the elevators that would take them up into the bustling trading hub.
The elevator carried them upward in a smooth, quiet ascent.
When the doors opened, the three of them stepped out into the main concourse of the Prime Stock Trading Hub. High glass ceilings let the morning light pour down in clean, bright shafts.

The air carried a mix of fresh produce, roasted coffee, and the faint metallic tang of the cold-storage sections further back. People moved with purpose, shoppers, vendors, delivery staff, yet the space still felt open and unhurried.
Stan guided Maya and Sophie toward the elevated eatery that overlooked the central trading floor.
The restaurant was already half-full with early patrons, but a corner table near the glass railing was free. He gestured towards it, and they walked to the table and sat.

The view below showed the busy flow of the hub: crates of specialty produce being wheeled past, glass cases of aged meats gleaming under careful lighting, shelves of imported goods stretching into the distance.

A server appeared almost at once. They ordered simply, freshly baked bread still warm from the oven, soft scrambled eggs with herbs, smoked salmon, a pot of strong coffee, and a small selection of tropical fruit.
While they waited, Maya rested her chin in one hand and looked at Stan with a slow, appreciative smile.
"You show up looking like that first thing in the morning and expect us to behave?" she teased, her voice low enough that only the three of them could hear. "Dangerous strategy."

Sophie leaned in slightly, her knee brushing Stan’s under the table. "She’s right. You’re sitting there looking completely put-together after last night, while I’m still thinking about how good your hands felt on me in the shower this morning." Her eyes sparkled with quiet mischief. "It’s unfair."

Stan’s mouth curved. "I’ll take the criticism. Especially when it comes with the two of you looking like that." His gaze moved briefly over the soft neckline of Maya’s dress, then the way Sophie’s top sat against her curves. "Makes the morning better.
Maya’s foot found his under the table, the light pressure of her toes deliberately playful. "Keep talking like that and we might decide the shopping can wait."
The food arrived before either of them could escalate the thought. Plates were set down with quiet efficiency.

The scrambled eggs were rich and fragrant; the bread tore open in soft, steaming pieces; the salmon was delicate and perfectly smoked. A platter of sliced tropical fruit added a burst of color to the table, while the freshly brewed coffee filled the air with a rich, inviting aroma.
They ate at an unhurried pace, the conversation drifting between soft remarks about the food and more personal, lingering observations.

Maya speared a piece of pineapple and popped it into her mouth, humming softly at the sweetness. Sophie wrapped both hands around her coffee cup, taking a slow sip before reaching for another piece of bread.

Sophie buttered the piece of bread and held it out for Stan to take a bite directly from her fingers. When he did, her eyes lingered on his mouth a moment longer than necessary. "You know," she murmured, "I could get used to feeding you in public too. There’s something very satisfying about it."

Maya laughed under her breath, spearing a piece of fruit and offering it across the table in the same way. "Careful. If we start competing over who gets to spoil him more, the poor man won’t stand a chance."
Stan accepted the fruit, then reached beneath the table to give Maya’s knee a brief, warm squeeze. "I’m not complaining. In fact, I think I could get used to this level of attention."
They continued like that, small shared bites, quiet laughter, the occasional brush of fingers or knees under the table.
The eatery around them stayed busy, but their corner felt private, wrapped in the easy intimacy they had carried from the night before and the soft morning drive.

By the time the last of the coffee was gone and the plates were cleared, a comfortable fullness settled over them. Maya leaned back in her chair with a contented sigh, one hand resting lightly on her stomach.
"That was perfect," she said. "Now I actually feel ready to face the rest of this place."
Sophie stretched gracefully, the motion making the fabric of her top shift in ways that briefly drew Stan’s eye. "Agreed. Let’s go make sure your kitchen stops looking so neglected."
Stan stood and offered a hand to each of them in turn.
As they rose, Maya’s fingers lingered in his a second longer than needed; Sophie’s shoulder brushed his chest as she stepped close.
The server returned with the bill, and Stan settled it without a second thought.

The three of them left the eatery together, the warmth of the shared meal and the quiet, teasing affection still hanging pleasantly between them as they stepped back onto the main floor of the trading hub, ready to begin the rest of their morning.
