Not the kind of place most people think of for everyday shopping, but they carry everything, high-quality produce, specialty cuts, imported goods, household staples.
One stop and the house will be properly stocked for a while."
Maya’s fingers gave his thigh a light, appreciative squeeze.
"A whole trading hub just to restock your kitchen?
You really don’t do anything halfway, do you?"
"Wouldn’t want my two favorite guests going hungry," he answered, voice low and warm.
"Or me, for that matter."
Sophie laughed softly, the sound intimate in the quiet cabin of the car.
"Listen to him.
Acting like we didn’t just spend half the night making sure he was thoroughly taken care of." Her fingertips traced a slow line along the side of his neck.
"Though I suppose feeding him is the next responsible step."
Maya leaned a little closer, her soft breast brushing against his arm as she spoke.
"Responsible and enjoyable.
I like the combination." She glanced out the window, then back at him with a playful glint in her eyes.
"Just don’t get too distracted by all the options once we’re inside.
I’d rather not lose you to a particularly impressive cut of steak."
Stan chuckled, the sound low in his chest.
"I’ll try to restrain myself.
But no promises if they have those aged wagyu portions you both like."
"Bribery already?" Sophie teased, her voice rich with amusement.
"We’re not even there yet and he’s already planning to spoil us."
"Can you blame me?" he replied, glancing briefly at Maya before checking the mirror to catch Sophie’s reflection.
"I have excellent taste in company.
It tends to extend to everything else."
Maya’s thumb resumed its slow circles.
"Mm.
Flattery and fine food.
Dangerous combination this early in the morning."
Sophie rested her chin more firmly against the headrest, smiling.
"Dangerous in the best way.
I’m already curious what else he’s going to try to talk us into once we’re walking those aisles."
"Nothing you won’t enjoy," Stan said, the corner of his mouth lifting.
"I promise."
The conversation flowed easily after that, soft, affectionate remarks, quiet laughter, the occasional lingering touch.
Maya’s hand never left his thigh for long; Sophie’s fingers continued their gentle exploration of the short hair at the back of his neck.
The enclosed space of the car held the faint, clean scent of the soap they had shared that morning, mixed with the subtle warmth of their nice feminine perfume.

After another few turns through quieter streets, the large modern structure of the Prime Stock Trading Hub came into view, glass and steel rising cleanly against the morning sky, its broad entrance already seeing a steady stream of early shoppers and delivery vehicles.
Stan guided the Audi into the underground parking levels, the engine’s soft purr echoing briefly off the concrete walls as he found a space near the elevators.
He put the car in park and killed the engine.
For a moment the three of them simply sat there, the quiet intimacy of the drive still lingering between them.
Maya gave his thigh one last slow stroke before withdrawing her hand with a small, satisfied smile.
"Well... shall we go make sure our king’s kitchen is worthy of him again?"
Sophie was already reaching for her door handle, eyes bright.
"Lead the way."
Stan stepped out, the cool underground air brushing his skin.
Sophie and Maya stepped out as well.
With that they walked together toward the elevators that would take them up into the bustling trading hub.
The elevator carried them upward in a smooth, quiet ascent.
When the doors opened, the three of them stepped out into the main concourse of the Prime Stock Trading Hub.
High glass ceilings let the morning light pour down in clean, bright shafts.
The air carried a mix of fresh produce, roasted coffee, and the faint metallic tang of the cold-storage sections further back.
People moved with purpose, shoppers, vendors, delivery staff, yet the space still felt open and unhurried.
Stan guided Maya and Sophie toward the elevated eatery that overlooked the central trading floor.
The restaurant was already half-full with early patrons, but a corner table near the glass railing was free.
He gestured towards it, and they walked to the table and sat.

The view below showed the busy flow of the hub: crates of specialty produce being wheeled past, glass cases of aged meats gleaming under careful lighting, shelves of imported goods stretching into the distance.
A server appeared almost at once.
They ordered simply, freshly baked bread still warm from the oven, soft scrambled eggs with herbs, smoked salmon, a pot of strong coffee, and a small selection of tropical fruit.
While they waited, Maya rested her chin in one hand and looked at Stan with a slow, appreciative smile.
"You show up looking like that first thing in the morning and expect us to behave?" she teased, her voice low enough that only the three of them could hear.
"Dangerous strategy."
Sophie leaned in slightly, her knee brushing Stan’s under the table.
"She’s right.

You’re sitting there looking completely put-together after last night, while I’m still thinking about how good your hands felt on me in the shower this morning." Her eyes sparkled with quiet mischief.
"It’s unfair."
Stan’s mouth curved.
"I’ll take the criticism.
Especially when it comes with the two of you looking like that." His gaze moved briefly over the soft neckline of Maya’s dress, then the way Sophie’s top sat against her curves.
"Makes the morning better.
Maya’s foot found his under the table, the light pressure of her toes deliberately playful.
"Keep talking like that and we might decide the shopping can wait."
The food arrived before either of them could escalate the thought.
Plates were set down with quiet efficiency.
The scrambled eggs were rich and fragrant; the bread tore open in soft, steaming pieces; the salmon was delicate and perfectly smoked.
A platter of sliced tropical fruit added a burst of color to the table, while the freshly brewed coffee filled the air with a rich, inviting aroma.
They ate at an unhurried pace, the conversation drifting between soft remarks about the food and more personal, lingering observations.
Maya speared a piece of pineapple and popped it into her mouth, humming softly at the sweetness.
Sophie wrapped both hands around her coffee cup, taking a slow sip before reaching for another piece of bread.
Sophie buttered the piece of bread and held it out for Stan to take a bite directly from her fingers.
When he did, her eyes lingered on his mouth a moment longer than necessary.
"You know," she murmured, "I could get used to feeding you in public too.
There’s something very satisfying about it."
Maya laughed under her breath, spearing a piece of fruit and offering it across the table in the same way.
"Careful.
If we start competing over who gets to spoil him more, the poor man won’t stand a chance."
Stan accepted the fruit, then reached beneath the table to give Maya’s knee a brief, warm squeeze.
"I’m not complaining.
In fact, I think I could get used to this level of attention."
They continued like that, small shared bites, quiet laughter, the occasional brush of fingers or knees under the table.
The eatery around them stayed busy, but their corner felt private, wrapped in the easy intimacy they had carried from the night before and the soft morning drive.
By the time the last of the coffee was gone and the plates were cleared, a comfortable fullness settled over them.
Maya leaned back in her chair with a contented sigh, one hand resting lightly on her stomach.
"That was perfect," she said.
"Now I actually feel ready to face the rest of this place."
Sophie stretched gracefully, the motion making the fabric of her top shift in ways that briefly drew Stan’s eye.
"Agreed.
Let’s go make sure your kitchen stops looking so neglected."
Stan stood and offered a hand to each of them in turn.
As they rose, Maya’s fingers lingered in his a second longer than needed; Sophie’s shoulder brushed his chest as she stepped close.
The server returned with the bill, and Stan settled it without a second thought.

The three of them left the eatery together, the warmth of the shared meal and the quiet, teasing affection still hanging pleasantly between them as they stepped back onto the main floor of the trading hub, ready to begin the rest of their morning.

chapters.title: Chapter 391: It’s Alright
paragraphs: They spent the next hour moving through the Prime Stock Trading Hub with easy purpose. Stan selected practical staples and higher-end ingredients with the same quiet efficiency he brought to most things; Maya and Sophie added their own preferences, fresh herbs, specialty cheeses, the particular cut of meat they both liked, a few bottles of the rice wine they had brought him the night before. Soft conversation and light touches threaded through the shopping: Maya’s fingers brushing his when they both reached for the same item, Sophie leaning close to murmur a suggestion against his ear, the occasional shared glance that carried the lingering warmth of the morning.

By the time they finished, two large insulated bags and several sturdy paper sacks held everything the house needed. They carried the load together down to the underground garage. Stan opened the boot of the Audi and packed the bags with careful precision, making sure nothing would shift during the drive. Maya stood close enough that her shoulder brushed his as she handed him the last item; Sophie waited by the passenger door, watching them with a soft, contented expression.

Once the boot closed with a solid thud, the three of them settled into the car. Stan had just started the engine when Maya’s phone chimed. She glanced at the screen, then answered, holding the device slightly away from her ear so the others could hear.
A polite but urgent voice came through clearly.

"Miss Maya, I’m sorry to disturb you this early, but we have a situation at the company. The quality-control team just flagged an issue with the latest production batch. It’s not a safety concern, but the entire shipment has been put on hold until you personally approve how we proceed. The production manager and the head of quality control are waiting for you in the conference room."
Maya’s expression shifted into a mild, apologetic smile as she looked at Stan. "Something came up..."
Stan glanced at her, one hand still resting on the wheel. "It’s not been long since you started. How has it been going?"

"The company is still in its beginning phase," she answered, voice calm but already carrying a quiet professionalism, "but it’s doing well. Better than I expected, actually." She listened for another moment, then spoke into the phone. "Tell them I’ll be there shortly. Have the full report ready."
She ended the call and exhaled softly, turning toward Stan with a small, rueful look. "I’m sorry. I was looking forward to the rest of the morning with both of you."
Sophie leaned forward from the back seat and gave Maya’s shoulder a light, reassuring squeeze. "Work happens. We’ll still be here when you’re done.
Stan simply nodded, already shifting the car into gear. "Direct me."

Maya guided him through a series of turns that took them away from the busier commercial districts and into a quieter industrial-adjacent area. After several minutes the low, modern building that housed her young company came into view, clean lines of glass and pale concrete, a discreet sign near the entrance, the kind of place that still carried the energy of something newly built and ambitious. Stan had invested in it only days earlier; seeing it now, already active enough to require her personal attention, brought a quiet sense of satisfaction.
He pulled into a visitor space near the main doors. Maya unbuckled, then leaned across the center console and pressed a soft, lingering kiss to his lips.
"Thank you for understanding," she murmured. "I won’t be longer than I have to."
Sophie smiled from the back. "Go be the boss. We’ll keep your seat warm."
Sophie’s words weren’t offensive and Maya didn’t take offense...

Maya gave them both one last warm look, then stepped out of the car and walked toward the entrance with steady, purposeful strides. Stan and Sophie watched her disappear inside before the quiet of the parked Audi settled around them once more.
Sophie shifted forward from the back seat, resting her arms lightly on the center console so she could look at Stan more directly. A soft, regretful smile touched her lips.
"I have an urgent lecture I can’t miss," she said. "I should get going too."

Stan turned his head toward her, the corner of his mouth lifting in an easy, affectionate smile. "Go study well, then. Become a great nurse for me." His voice warmed. "I’ll never forget how you treated my hand that night, after I punched the bastard who tried to assault you. And his guards."

Sophie’s expression softened with memory. She reached out and brushed her fingers lightly along the back of his hand where it rested on the gearshift. "Those were some nice moves," she murmured, a quiet note of lingering admiration in her voice. "And that immense power... I still find it unbelievable that you handled that many men alone so easily.
Stan gave a low, amused laugh. "Well... I’m not weak."

Sophie’s eyes sparkled. "No. You’re definitely not." She settled back into her seat as he started the engine again, but she kept her body angled toward him. As the car pulled out of the lot and joined the morning traffic, her hand found his thigh once more, resting there with familiar warmth. "You know, most men would have needed help that night. Or at least looked a little shaken afterward. You just... handled it. And then let me fuss over your knuckles like it was nothing."
"I liked the fussing," Stan admitted, glancing at her with a small, genuine smile. "Especially from you."

Sophie made a soft, pleased sound. "Careful. Keep saying things like that and I might start finding excuses to check you for injuries more often." Her fingers traced a slow, idle circle on his thigh. "Even if there aren’t any."

The drive to her place was unhurried. Conversation drifted between quiet teasing and softer reminiscence, how everything had felt chaotic when he went to get drinks until he stepped in, how strangely calm he had been afterward, how she had been equal parts impressed and worried while she cleaned the small cuts on his hand. Stan listened more than he spoke, occasionally answering with a low chuckle or a brief, warm remark that made Sophie’s smile linger.

When they finally pulled up outside her building, Sophie unbuckled and leaned across the console. She kissed him slowly, thoroughly, one hand resting against his cheek. The kiss carried the lingering intimacy of the night before and the quiet affection of the morning, soft, unhurried, and full of unspoken apology.

When she drew back, her forehead rested lightly against his for a moment. "I’m sorry I couldn’t stay with you the whole day," she whispered. "Especially after you were off-grid and unreachable for more than three days. I kept wondering if everything was all right."
Stan’s hand came up to cradle the side of her neck, thumb brushing gently along her jaw. "It’s nothing to worry about," he said, voice steady and warm. "You’re here now. That’s enough."

Sophie smiled, gave him one last brief kiss, then stepped out of the car. She paused on the sidewalk to wave before disappearing into the building. Stan watched until the door closed behind her, then sat for a moment longer in the quiet of the Audi, the faint scent of her perfume still lingering in the cabin, before finally putting the car back into gear

chapters.title: Chapter 392: A Vampire’s Curiosity
paragraphs: Stan drove back through the quieting streets, the Audi’s engine a low, steady hum. He parked in his usual spot in the underground garage and stepped out. After storing everything he had bought at the Hub in his inventory, he walked toward the elevators.
He stopped just short of the doors, however, and tilted his head upward, eyes half-lidded as his senses stretched.
Camilla was back. She was on the roof of the building, exactly where she had settled the night before.
A faint smile ghosted across his mouth. He remained still, waiting.

Above, Camilla felt the brush of his awareness. For a moment she stayed where she was, crimson eyes narrowed at the empty blue sky. Then, with a silent push of her feet, she left the roof. Her descent was unhurried, almost languid; she drifted downward as though gravity itself had politely stepped aside. No rush of air, no sound. She simply lowered herself through the open space until her boots touched the concrete beside him without the slightest noise.
She stood there for a beat, posture straight, chin slightly lifted.
"You seem to be having a lot of fun..."
The words were delivered in the same cool, faintly accusing tone she had used the previous night. Jealousy sat just beneath the surface, carefully masked and yet not quite hidden.
Stan almost smiled. He kept his expression mild. "Well... yeah."
Camilla’s gaze lingered on his face longer than necessary. Then, as if catching herself, she looked sharply to the side. A small, unconscious pout tugged at her lower lip.
Stan spoke casually, as though commenting on the weather. "Where have you been? I couldn’t sense you when I woke up."
She folded her arms loosely, still not looking at him. "Well, I’m having fun just like you did all night long with your ’girls’"
The words were deliberately airy, as though she had been out enjoying herself rather than simply watching the moon and stars at night and wandering during the morning in restless silence.
Stan’s eyes flicked briefly toward the upper floors. "And staying on the roof like that... what if somebody saw you?"

Camilla finally glanced back at him, a spark of pride in her crimson eyes. "My aura and my presence were fully suppressed, both while I was up there and while I was coming down. If I don’t wish to be noticed, no new-age human or any of their little toys can detect me."
Stan gave a small nod. "Good.
It seemed she had finally begun to understand his reasoning she never understood before...

Without another word Camilla stepped into the open elevator. The restless energy around her was still palpable, tightly controlled but not entirely hidden. Stan followed, pressed the button for his floor, and the doors slid shut. The cabin began its smooth ascent.
For a while neither of them spoke. Only when Stan had quietly confirmed there were no cameras did he break the silence.
"So... what do you think of Earth so far?"
Camilla kept her eyes on the glowing floor indicator. A soft, dismissive sound left her throat.
"Hmph. No matter what toys they come up with, ants will always be ants. Even if some of those toys are... a little interesting."
Stan’s mouth twitched. He forced the smile to stay mild and turned his gaze forward again.
’I guess it’s going to take some time for her to change that perspective.’

The elevator chimed softly as it reached his floor. The doors slid open, and the two of them stepped out into the quiet hallway before Stan unlocked the apartment and pushed the door wide. They entered without ceremony.

Camilla’s gaze drifted almost immediately to the large bed against the far wall. The sheets were freshly changed, the surface smooth and undisturbed, yet her mind filled in every detail of the night before with unwelcome clarity. Sophie’s arched back. Maya’s soft moans. The way Stan’s hands had gripped and guided. The wet sounds, the low groans, the way both women had looked at him afterward with such open, sated affection.
A faint warmth rose in her cheeks before she even realized it. She turned her face slightly away and drew a slow, deliberate breath.
’Calm down, Camilla. Calm down. Don’t get riled up over this...’
Across the room, Stan paused just inside the doorway as a translucent panel of text flickered across his vision.
[Side Mission Completed.]
[Objective: Travel to Antarctica.]
[Status: Completed]
[You’ve gained the Profession Skill Chef (Master).]
[+20% Proficiency when cooking...]
Knowledge flooded in at once, techniques, ratios, timing, the subtle differences between ordinary ingredients and those that carried residual energy.

Mundane mastery settled into his mind with crystalline clarity, followed by more specialized fragments: methods for preparing Qi-infused beasts, mutant flesh, even a handful of dishes that carried an oddly familiar resonance, as though they might appeal to something beyond human tastes. Compared to the Pilot mastery he had once received, this felt deeper, broader, more immediately useful.
He glanced toward Camilla.
She caught the look at once. Her eyes narrowed slightly, and she turned her face further to the side, arms loosely folded.
"What?"
Stan’s mouth curved in a mild, unbothered smile. "Care to eat good food?"
The question made the memories of the previous night flicker through her mind again. She kept her gaze firmly averted, chin lifting a fraction in practiced indifference.
"None of these new-age human dishes interest me," she said coolly. "Human blood is the best delicacy there is."
Stan’s smile didn’t fade. "Don’t worry. You’ll be surprised."

Camilla gave a small, noncommittal shrug, still not looking at him. Curiosity tugged at her despite the sharp words, and she made no move to leave or object. If he wanted to waste time cooking, that was his business. She simply happened to be... present.
Stan took that as acceptance enough. Still faintly amused, and more than a little eager to test the new skill, he turned and walked toward the kitchen.

Compared to the Pilot mastery he had once received, this felt deeper, broader, more immediately useful.
He glanced toward Camilla.
She caught the look at once.
Her eyes narrowed slightly, and she turned her face further to the side, arms loosely folded.
"What?"
Stan’s mouth curved in a mild, unbothered smile.
"Care to eat good food?"
The question made the memories of the previous night flicker through her mind again.
She kept her gaze firmly averted, chin lifting a fraction in practiced indifference.
"None of these new-age human dishes interest me," she said coolly.
"Human blood is the best delicacy there is."
Stan’s smile didn’t fade.
"Don’t worry.
You’ll be surprised."
Camilla gave a small, noncommittal shrug, still not looking at him.
Curiosity tugged at her despite the sharp words, and she made no move to leave or object.
If he wanted to waste time cooking, that was his business.
She simply happened to be... present.
Stan took that as acceptance enough.
Still faintly amused, and more than a little eager to test the new skill, he turned and walked toward the kitchen.

chapters.title: Chapter 393: The Aroma Of Temptation
paragraphs: Stan stepped into the kitchen and set a few basic tools on the counter, cutting boards, a heavy pan, a small selection of spices. For a moment he simply stood there, considering.
’What should I call this new dish I’m inventing... something a vampire like Camilla might actually enjoy?’
He exhaled quietly. ’Let’s see. The ingredients are all parts of the polar bear I took down and stored in my inventory...’
A decision settled cleanly in his mind. ’Bloodless Crimson Feast.’

Liver, kidney, bone marrow, heart, and a modest cut of the denser muscle meat. It would have been better if some of the blood had remained, but the Blood Fang daggers had drained every drop the instant they opened the creature’s throat.

With a thought, the massive polar-bear carcass materialized on the open kitchen floor, cold and motionless. A second thought brought the paired Blood Fang daggers into his palms. The intricate red patterns along the blades glowed faintly as he knelt and began to work.
The newly gained Chef (Master) skill settled into his hands like instinct. Every motion was precise, almost elegant.

He opened the chest cavity with a single clean stroke, lifted free the deep-red liver, the dense heart, and a carefully measured portion of kidney. Bone marrow was scooped from the sliced long bones in neat, glossy segments.
A thin layer of the rich subcutaneous fat was set aside to render. Even the small amount of muscle meat came away without ragged edges. In barely six minutes the counter held exactly what he needed.
The floor remained spotless. The remainder of the carcass vanished back into his inventory as though it had never been there.
Stan straightened and rolled his shoulders once.

He was not cooking this solely for Camilla. He was curious himself. Polar-bear liver carried dangerous levels of vitamin A for ordinary humans, but his tempered body and cultivation base would handle it without issue. So he just wanted to know how this newly invented dish would taste.
His gaze moved over the prepared ingredients as the plan formed with quiet clarity.
The liver would be the foundation, rich, intensely mineral. The heart would add dense, meaty depth.

Only a small amount of kidney; its flavor was too aggressive in larger quantities. Bone marrow would lend a silky, luxurious texture, while the rendered fat would carry everything and keep the liver from turning dry. Black garlic for subtle sweetness and complexity. A few Arctic wild herbs to cut through the heaviness. Salt. The barest touch of spice.
Finally his eyes settled on the small vial of liquid Qi he had set aside.
Just a little.
That alone should be enough to lift the entire dish far beyond ordinary cuisine.
"With liquid Qi mixed into it," Stan murmured, almost to himself, "this should become proper Qi-rich food."

A faint smile touched his mouth. Even a modest amount of liquid Qi would multiply the flavor several times over, possibly turning an already exceptional meal into something that simply could not exist in the mundane world.
He stared at the array on the counter. Liver. Heart. Kidney. Marrow. Not a single drop of blood. His weapons had seen to that.
A brief pause, then the smile returned, sharper this time.
’Fine. If I don’t have blood, I’ll make something close enough.’

A soft shift of air told him he was no longer alone. Camilla had approached without sound and now stood a short distance away, arms loosely folded, crimson eyes fixed on the counter with carefully neutral interest. When she realized he had noticed her, she looked pointedly to the side, chin lifting a fraction.
Stan glanced at her, still wearing a faint smile. "Curious after all?"
"Hmph." She kept her gaze averted. "I’m merely making sure you don’t set the place on fire with whatever strange thing you’re attempting."
Her words were cool, almost dismissive, yet she made no move to leave.
Stan smiled.

He could tell she didn’t actually mean that. After all, since last night, she had been trying so hard to hide and suppress the feelings that had begun to bloom within her, the interest and favorability she had developed toward him, feelings that were becoming increasingly difficult for even her to ignore.
Sighing, Stan turned back to the counter without further comment and set to work.

He rendered the polar-bear fat first over medium heat until it turned clear and fragrant. Into the shimmering fat went the diced black garlic, followed moments later by the finely chopped Arctic herbs. The kitchen filled with a deep, savory scent that was already richer than ordinary cooking. Camilla’s nose twitched once before she caught herself and looked away, arms still folded.

Stan worked with quiet, unhurried precision. The liver was sliced into even, thick pieces and seared just long enough to develop a dark crust while remaining soft inside. The heart followed, cut into dense cubes and browned until the edges caramelized.

Only a small amount of the kidney went in; all minced almost to a paste so its aggressive flavor would season rather than dominate. Bone marrow was added last, melting into the mixture and giving everything a glossy, luxurious sheen.

Camilla watched from the corner of her eye despite herself. Every motion of his hands was clean, confident, almost elegant. There was none of the clumsy trial-and-error she expected from someone who had only just acquired the skill. He moved like someone who had cooked this dish a hundred times.
"Hmmph...’ she acted cold, yet she did not look away for long.

The aroma continued to deepen. Rich mineral notes from the liver, the deep meatiness of the heart, the silky undertone of marrow, all balanced by the subtle sweetness of black garlic and the sharp brightness of the herbs. Camilla’s mouth watered before she could stop it. She pressed her lips together and turned her face further toward the window, pretending interest in the morning sunlight.
Stan glanced at her once, a faint smile touching his mouth, but said nothing.

chapters.title: Chapter 394: The Wave Has Arrived
paragraphs: Stan glanced at her once, a faint smile touching his mouth as he saw her trying hard not to acknowledge the nice aroma, he said nothing but reach into his inventory and withdrew something out... Two drops of liquid Qi fell into the pot.
The effect was immediate.

The aroma that rose from the pan intensified several times over, thicker, richer, almost alive. It carried a subtle, resonant depth that ordinary food could never possess, as though the very air had gained weight and sweetness at once. The scent curled through the kitchen and wrapped around them both.

Camilla’s eyes widened for the briefest moment. Her fingers tightened on her arms. The sudden surge of fragrance made her throat tighten with unwilling hunger. She looked sharply away again, but the damage was done.
"...What did you just add?" she asked, voice carefully flat.
"A little liquid Qi," Stan answered mildly, stirring the contents of the pan. "Just enough."
Camilla made a quiet, dismissive sound in her throat. "Hmph. Using something like that on mere ingredients... wasteful."

Yet she remained exactly where she was, crimson eyes fixed on the simmering pan despite her words. The rich, impossible scent continued to fill the kitchen, and her carefully maintained indifference was beginning to crack at the edges.

Stan tasted a small portion, nodded once in satisfaction, and began plating the dish with the same quiet precision he had shown throughout. The final result sat on the counter in two deep bowls, dark, glossy, fragrant, and far more than ordinary food.
He looked at Camilla and tilted his head slightly.
"Still uninterested?"

Stan held her gaze for a moment longer, still faintly smiling, then simply shook his head and portioned the second bowl. He carried both to the dining table, set one in front of the empty chair opposite him, and sat down with his own. The rich, complex aroma rose between them.

Camilla remained standing a moment longer, arms still loosely crossed. Pride warred with the undeniable pull of the scent. At last she exhaled through her nose, walked over with deliberate nonchalance, and sat. She picked up the utensil he had placed beside the bowl, lifted a small piece of the glossy liver, and placed it in her mouth.

The flavor unfolded at once, deep, mineral richness from the polar-bear liver, balanced by the dense, almost buttery depth of the heart. The marrow melted across her tongue in a silky wave, carrying the subtle sweetness of black garlic and the bright, cleansing note of the Arctic herbs.

Beneath it all ran something else entirely, a clean, resonant power from the liquid Qi that made every component taste sharper, fuller, more alive than ordinary food had any right to be. It was not blood, yet it satisfied a similar craving in a way she had not expected.
Camilla chewed slowly, then swallowed. Her expression remained carefully composed, but a faint color touched the tops of her cheeks.
"What’s there to brag about," she said at last, voice cool. "I guess you’re a pretty good chef..."
She looked sharply to the side, lips pressed into a small, unconscious pout.
Stan ate a bite of his own portion, the same layered intensity spreading across his tongue, and gave a quiet hum of satisfaction. "High praise, coming from you."

"It wasn’t praise," she muttered, still not looking at him. She took another bite anyway, larger this time, then another. The rich, Qi-infused flavors kept drawing her back. Each mouthful delivered the same surprising depth, the mineral weight of the liver, the meaty satisfaction of the heart, the luxurious melt of marrow, all lifted by that faint, electric resonance of liquid Qi. It was nothing like human blood, yet it scratched an itch she had not realized could be scratched by anything else.

They ate in relative silence for a while. Camilla kept her eyes on her bowl, determined not to give him the satisfaction of watching her enjoy it too openly. Every so often she would pause, as if remembering herself, and force her expression back into mild indifference, only to take another bite a moment later.
Stan spoke mildly between mouthfuls. "The liquid Qi makes a difference, doesn’t it?"
Camilla’s chopsticks hovered for half a second. "...It’s acceptable," she said at last, the words clipped. "For something that isn’t blood."
He only smiled and continued eating.

By the time their bowls were nearly empty, Camilla had abandoned any pretense of restraint. She finished the last glossy piece of heart, then used a fragment of the seared liver to wipe up the remaining sauce. Only when the bowl was completely clean did she set her chopsticks down with a quiet click.
Stan finished his own final bite a moment later and leaned back slightly, satisfied.

Camilla glanced at the empty bowl in front of her, then away again. A faint, residual warmth lingered on her tongue, rich, complex, and still faintly humming with the aftertaste of liquid Qi. She folded her arms once more, chin lifting.
"...Don’t expect me to say it was better than blood," she said, the words edged with stubborn pride. "But... it wasn’t terrible."
Stan’s quiet chuckle was the only reply he gave. ...
Stan’s quiet chuckle faded the moment he noticed the change in Camilla.

She was no longer looking at her empty bowl or pointedly away from him. Her crimson eyes had locked toward the south, sharp and utterly serious. The usual edge of pride and reluctance was gone, replaced by something colder and more focused, an alertness that bordered on readiness for battle.
He set his chopsticks down. "What’s wrong?"
Camilla’s voice came calm and even, almost detached. "It’s coming."
Stan studied her face. "What’s that?"
"The wave of Qi from Antarctica," she answered without looking away from the southern horizon. "It’s reaching this region."

At that moment, a soft ding sounded in Stan’s mind, audible only to him. A translucent system panel unfolded across his vision, displaying a map of the Earth. A faint, luminous tide crawled outward from the frozen continent, spreading across the globe in slow, inexorable waves of pale blue light.
A heartbeat later, he felt it.

chapters.title: Chapter 395: A Meeting Of Two Worlds
paragraphs: A heartbeat later, he felt it.

An invisible force washed through the apartment, through the walls, through the furniture, through his own body, and continued onward without resistance. In its wake the air itself changed. What had been ordinary, empty space now carried a subtle density, a faint pressure against the skin and lungs, like the atmosphere just before a storm. Qi had arrived. For the first time, the room itself could support normal cultivation.

Stan felt the difference first as texture. The air in his living room was fractionally heavier, richer, almost tangible. Camilla felt it too. She rose without a word, crossed to the balcony doors, and stepped outside. There she stood perfectly still, crimson eyes fixed on the city spread below, as though listening to something only she could hear, the slow, gathering pulse of a world beginning to change.

Stan pulled out his phone and checked the major news feeds. Nothing. No alerts, no strange reports, no mention of atmospheric anomalies. The world remained completely ignorant, still going about its ordinary business under an ordinary sky.

He sat back, the weight of that knowledge settling over him. He was one of the very few who understood what had just occurred. Camilla’s earlier warnings about Qi mutating animals rose in his mind. If the tide continued to spread and thicken, the changes would not remain subtle for long. The first signs would appear in the wild, then in the cities, and by the time ordinary people noticed, it would already be too late to pretend the world was still the same.
At the balcony, Camilla’s posture remained alert, almost regal. Whatever the full implications of the Qi wave were, she clearly understood them better than she had chosen to say aloud.

Stan closed his eyes briefly and checked his internal state. The Genesis Realm base within him was already responding, drawing in the new ambient Qi passively, steadily, like a dry riverbed finally receiving rain. Cultivation on Earth no longer required him to rely solely on the reserves stored in his inventory. The planet itself had begun to provide.
He opened his eyes and looked toward the still figure on the balcony.
"It’s starting, huh?" he said quietly.
Camilla’s head inclined in a small, unconscious nod, the gesture of a comrade acknowledging shared understanding rather than a superior addressing an inferior.
The moment of quiet recognition lasted only a few seconds.
Then the doorbell rang.
It rang a second time, more insistent.
Stan looked at Camilla. "Do you plan to hide your presence?"
She lifted her chin a fraction, crimson eyes cool. "No. I don’t want to. It’s beneath me to hide my presence from ants."
Stan’s expression hardened just enough to make the words land with weight. "Those I care about are not ants.

Camilla held his gaze for a long moment. The seriousness in his eyes was unmistakable, steady, protective, and absolute. At last she looked aside and let out a quiet sigh, the first small concession she had made since the Qi wave arrived. "...I guess so. Won’t you check who’s at the door?"
He did not ask her again. If it was one of the women close to him, he was confident he could handle whatever followed. With a small inward breath he walked to the entrance and opened the door.
Sacha stood there, bright and familiar, a smile already on her face.
"You’re surprised by my visit, right?" she teased, eyes sparkling with playful satisfaction.
Stan’s expression softened into a genuine smile. "Yes, I am."
She winked. "You’re always the one visiting me every Sunday, so I decided to reverse it this time."
"It’s all good." He stepped aside to let her in. "So how have you been, Sis? Work and everything?"

Sacha’s face lit up as she entered, the usual easy warmth between them returning at once. "Everything’s going smoothly. I can never thank you enough for giving me that job and position. With me managing the company, things have been moving fast, the stock’s risen a lot in a short time."
"That’s good to hear," Stan said, closing the door behind her. The ordinary conversation felt almost surreal against the lingering density of Qi still settling into the apartment.
Sacha walked into the living room and stopped.

Camilla sat to the side, posture composed, presence no longer veiled. The moment Sacha’s eyes landed on her, a faint, instinctive pressure settled over her, subtle yet unmistakable, like standing in the presence of something far above ordinary humanity. It was Camilla’s natural bloodline superiority, no longer suppressed. The sensation did not touch Stan, shielded as he was by the system, and it had been absent the previous night when Camilla had kept herself carefully hidden. Now it brushed against Sacha like a quiet, regal weight that made the air feel slightly heavier around her.
Sacha forced a polite smile and glanced at her brother, a flicker of unease crossing her features. "Who is she?"
Before Stan could answer, Camilla spoke first, a small, composed smile on her lips.
"You’re his sister?"
"Yes, I am," Sacha replied carefully, still trying to place the strange pressure she felt.
"It’s nice to meet you, then," Camilla said. "I’m his comrade."
Sacha’s brows drew together. She turned fully toward Stan, the word clearly sitting wrong with her.
Stan could read the look easily, ’Comrade? What kind of word is that?’
Sacha voiced it a second later, her tone polite but edged with quiet confusion. "Comrade? Isn’t ’friend’ or something better?"
Sacha’s question hung in the air, pointed and unmistakably protective.
Stan met his sister’s gaze with an easy calm. "It’s accurate," he said simply. "We’ve been through enough that ’friend’ doesn’t quite cover it."

Camilla remained seated, one leg crossed over the other, expression composed. The faint pressure of her presence still lingered in the room like a quiet, invisible weight. She glanced at Sacha, then away again, as though the matter were already settled.
"Comrade is sufficient," she said coolly. "I see no reason to dress it up further."

Sacha’s eyes flicked between the two of them. The word still sat strangely with her, but the quiet certainty in Stan’s voice and the unshakable composure of the woman in front of her made further argument feel useless for the moment. She forced a small, polite smile and nodded once.
"I see... All right." She turned fully toward Camilla and extended a hand out of habit. "I’m Sacha. It’s nice to meet you."
Camilla looked at the offered hand for a brief second. She did not take it immediately. Instead she inclined her head in a measured, almost regal gesture.
"Camilla."

The Genesis Realm base within him was already responding, drawing in the new ambient Qi passively, steadily, like a dry riverbed finally receiving rain.
Cultivation on Earth no longer required him to rely solely on the reserves stored in his inventory.
The planet itself had begun to provide.
He opened his eyes and looked toward the still figure on the balcony.
"It’s starting, huh?" he said quietly.
Camilla’s head inclined in a small, unconscious nod, the gesture of a comrade acknowledging shared understanding rather than a superior addressing an inferior.
The moment of quiet recognition lasted only a few seconds.
Then the doorbell rang.
It rang a second time, more insistent.
Stan looked at Camilla.
"Do you plan to hide your presence?"
She lifted her chin a fraction, crimson eyes cool.
"No.
I don’t want to.
It’s beneath me to hide my presence from ants."
Stan’s expression hardened just enough to make the words land with weight.
"Those I care about are not ants.
Camilla held his gaze for a long moment.
The seriousness in his eyes was unmistakable, steady, protective, and absolute.
At last she looked aside and let out a quiet sigh, the first small concession she had made since the Qi wave arrived.
"...I guess so.
Won’t you check who’s at the door?"
He did not ask her again.
If it was one of the women close to him, he was confident he could handle whatever followed.
With a small inward breath he walked to the entrance and opened the door.
Sacha stood there, bright and familiar, a smile already on her face.
"You’re surprised by my visit, right?" she teased, eyes sparkling with playful satisfaction.
Stan’s expression softened into a genuine smile.
"Yes, I am."
She winked.
"You’re always the one visiting me every Sunday, so I decided to reverse it this time."
"It’s all good." He stepped aside to let her in.
"So how have you been, Sis?
Work and everything?"
Sacha’s face lit up as she entered, the usual easy warmth between them returning at once.
"Everything’s going smoothly.
I can never thank you enough for giving me that job and position.
With me managing the company, things have been moving fast, the stock’s risen a lot in a short time."
"That’s good to hear," Stan said, closing the door behind her.
The ordinary conversation felt almost surreal against the lingering density of Qi still settling into the apartment.
Sacha walked into the living room and stopped.
Camilla sat to the side, posture composed, presence no longer veiled.
The moment Sacha’s eyes landed on her, a faint, instinctive pressure settled over her, subtle yet unmistakable, like standing in the presence of something far above ordinary humanity.
It was Camilla’s natural bloodline superiority, no longer suppressed.
The sensation did not touch Stan, shielded as he was by the system, and it had been absent the previous night when Camilla had kept herself carefully hidden.
Now it brushed against Sacha like a quiet, regal weight that made the air feel slightly heavier around her.
Sacha forced a polite smile and glanced at her brother, a flicker of unease crossing her features.
"Who is she?"
Before Stan could answer, Camilla spoke first, a small, composed smile on her lips.
"You’re his sister?"
"Yes, I am," Sacha replied carefully, still trying to place the strange pressure she felt.
"It’s nice to meet you, then," Camilla said.
"I’m his comrade."
Sacha’s brows drew together.
She turned fully toward Stan, the word clearly sitting wrong with her.
Stan could read the look easily, ’Comrade?
What kind of word is that?’
Sacha voiced it a second later, her tone polite but edged with quiet confusion.
"Comrade?
Isn’t ’friend’ or something better?"
Sacha’s question hung in the air, pointed and unmistakably protective.
Stan met his sister’s gaze with an easy calm.
"It’s accurate," he said simply.
"We’ve been through enough that ’friend’ doesn’t quite cover it."
Camilla remained seated, one leg crossed over the other, expression composed.
The faint pressure of her presence still lingered in the room like a quiet, invisible weight.
She glanced at Sacha, then away again, as though the matter were already settled.
"Comrade is sufficient," she said coolly.
"I see no reason to dress it up further."
Sacha’s eyes flicked between the two of them.
The word still sat strangely with her, but the quiet certainty in Stan’s voice and the unshakable composure of the woman in front of her made further argument feel useless for the moment.
She forced a small, polite smile and nodded once.
"I see...
All right." She turned fully toward Camilla and extended a hand out of habit.
"I’m Sacha.
It’s nice to meet you."
Camilla looked at the offered hand for a brief second.
She did not take it immediately.
Instead she inclined her head in a measured, almost regal gesture.
"Camilla."

chapters.title: Chapter 396: A Sister’s Suspicion
paragraphs: Camilla looked at the offered hand for a brief second. She did not take it at once. Instead she inclined her head in a measured, almost regal gesture.
"Camilla."

Only after that slight pause did she rise and accept the handshake. Her grip was cool and precise, lasting only as long as courtesy required before she released it and returned to her seat with the same unhurried composure.

Sacha withdrew her hand, the lingering sense of that faint suppression still brushing against her instincts like a soft pressure behind the eyes. She glanced at Stan again, searching his face for any further explanation, but he only gave her a mild, reassuring look and gestured toward the couch.
"Sit down, Sis. You came all this way. Want something to drink?"
Sacha hesitated a moment longer, then nodded and took a seat on the opposite side of the living room, keeping a careful distance from Camilla without making the choice obvious.

The atmosphere remained polite on the surface, yet a quiet undercurrent of assessment ran beneath it, Sacha still turning the word ’comrade’ over in her mind, and Camilla watching the exchange with the detached interest of someone who had already decided how much of herself she was willing to show.
Sacha settled onto the couch, but her attention soon drifted back to her brother. For the first time since arriving she truly looked at him.

Stan stood in a simple black singlet and shorts, the clean lines of muscle along his arms, shoulders, and chest fully visible. It was nothing she hadn’t seen before, yet something about him felt different.

Over the past few weeks he had changed in ways that still surprised her, rising from relative obscurity to become a major shareholder in both Wanhai and Star Entertainment, carrying himself with a new maturity that matched his sudden influence. But this was another layer entirely. His presence felt calmer, denser, more solid. Even his eyes seemed subtly altered, as though something quieter and heavier now lived behind them.
’Something about my brother feels different,’ she thought, frowning slightly without realizing it.
Stan noticed the prolonged stare and raised an eyebrow. "What is it? Something on my face?"
Sacha quickly shook her head. "It’s nothing.
’If I tell him I’m sensing all this, he’ll think I’ve lost it. I don’t even know how to explain it... it’s like he’s not entirely the same person I grew up with.’

Her gaze shifted toward Camilla again. The faint, instinctive pressure from earlier still brushed against her senses, the first time she had ever felt anything like it. Combined with the strangely dense, comfortable atmosphere of the apartment, it left her both curious and quietly protective.
She kept her tone light, almost casual. "How long have you known my brother?"
Camilla, still seated with perfect composure, answered without hesitation. "Not very long."
"And you live here?"
A brief pause. Camilla’s eyes flicked toward Stan, then away. "...No. Just sightseeing."
Sacha’s head turned toward her brother at once, the single word carrying a clear request for explanation.

Stan only met her look with mild calm, offering nothing further for the moment. The quiet tension between the three of them was unmistakable, Sacha trying to map out the exact nature of this "comrade," Camilla remaining proudly unconcerned with ordinary human expectations, and Stan standing in the middle of it all as though the situation were perfectly ordinary.
Then Sacha’s nose caught the lingering aroma still hanging in the air, rich, complex, and strangely compelling. She glanced toward the kitchen.
"Did you two cook something?"
Stan nodded. "Yeah."
"What was it?" she asked, genuine curiosity in her voice.

Stan’s expression tightened for a fraction of a second. ’Polar-bear liver. But I can’t tell her that. How do I even begin to explain where I got it? And I can’t serve her any of it either. The vitamin A content would be dangerous for her. She’s not like me or Camilla.’

He forced an easy smile. "Just some meat. We’ve already finished everything. I’ve still got some refrigerated meat left, though, I’ll cook something for you, Sis. My skills have improved a lot lately.
Sacha’s face brightened. "I can’t wait to test them, then. I want to see how much you’ve improved."

Across the room, Camilla’s crimson eyes locked onto Stan with quiet intensity. She could not understand why he was claiming the earlier meal was completely gone. The bowls had been emptied, yes, but the reason for the deliberate omission escaped her. She said nothing, only watched him with that same composed, faintly assessing gaze.
Stan gave his sister another mild smile and turned toward the kitchen. "Give me a few minutes."

Inside, he worked quickly and cleanly. He selected ordinary ingredients for safety, adding only a modest portion of the polar-bear muscle meat, nothing from the organs, and the smallest measured drop of liquid Qi. The Qi would be mild enough to benefit Sacha without any risk. The result would be flavorful, nourishing, and entirely safe.
As the pan began to heat and the first familiar scents rose, the quiet undercurrent of curiosity and unspoken questions continued to linger in the living room behind him.

Sacha leaned back slightly, arms folded, eyes moving between the closed kitchen doorway and the composed woman seated across from her. The apartment still felt... heavier than it should. Not oppressive. Simply denser, as if the air itself carried a weight she could almost lean against.

Camilla did not fill the silence. She sat with her spine straight, hands resting lightly in her lap, crimson gaze half-lidded yet fully aware. She had already taken Sacha’s measure during the handshake and the brief exchange that followed. The younger woman’s instincts were sharper than most, her wariness genuine rather than performative. Interesting. But not yet concerning.
Sacha broke the quiet first, voice still carefully casual. "He’s different lately."
Camilla’s eyes shifted toward her. "Is he."
It was not quite a question.
Sacha studied the other woman’s face for a moment, searching for any flicker of shared understanding, then looked away. "Yeah. He is."

In the kitchen, the sound of oil meeting hot metal rose softly. The scent that followed was warm and savory, layered with something cleaner and brighter than ordinary seasoning. Stan moved with practiced efficiency, every motion precise. He did not look back toward the living room. He already knew the shape of the silence waiting for him there.

chapters.title: Chapter 397: A Sister’s Misunderstanding
paragraphs: In the kitchen, Stan worked with quiet efficiency. He heated a clean pan and rendered a small amount of ordinary cooking oil, then added thin slices of the polar-bear muscle meat, nothing from the organs, alongside fresh vegetables, a touch of garlic, and a carefully measured drop of liquid Qi.
The Qi was diluted enough to be beneficial without any risk. The meat seared quickly, releasing a rich but approachable aroma that was far milder than the earlier dish.

Within minutes he had a balanced, fragrant plate ready: tender slices of meat over lightly seasoned greens and rice, the faint resonance of Qi woven so subtly into the flavors that only someone sensitive would notice it at all.
While he cooked, the living room fell into an uncomfortable silence.

Sacha shifted on the couch, glancing once toward Camilla, who sat with perfect stillness, crimson eyes half-lidded as though the entire situation barely warranted her attention. The lingering pressure of Camilla’s presence made the quiet feel heavier than it should have.
Finally Sacha forced an awkward smile. "So... what do you think of my brother?"
Camilla’s gaze drifted toward her, cool and assessing. "He’s pretty cool. Possesses plenty of interesting things. Makes me wonder if you have those too."
Sacha’s brows knit slightly. ’First "comrade," now "interesting things"... why does she talk like that? And what interesting things is she even talking about?’

She considered asking, then decided against it. The question felt too personal. For all she knew, her brother and this woman might share some private arrangement, possibly an intimate one, and the formal language might simply be their way of keeping it discreet.
She let the subject drop with another polite nod. Even though she had a slight smile as though she’ve figure them out...

Stan returned from the kitchen carrying the freshly prepared plate and set it in front of Sacha. "Here, Sis. Nothing complicated, but it’s pretty good I’m sure you’ll love it... Tell me what you think."

Sacha’s expression brightened at the familiar gesture. She picked up her utensils and took a bite, eyes widening slightly at the clean, satisfying flavor. "You’ve really improved. This is good, actually better than good. When did you start cooking like this?"
"Recently," Stan said, settling into the seat across from her. "I’ve had time to practice."
"Clearly." Sacha took another bite, then glanced toward Camilla. "Does she cook too, or is this all you?"
Camilla’s eyes opened a fraction wider, as if the question itself were mildly surprising. "I have little interest in cooking... Though I can try."
The reply was so serious, matter-of-fact and off at the same time that Sacha almost laughed. She covered it with a quick sip of water. "Right. Of course, it’s always good to try new things.

They exchanged a few light remarks about the food and her work at the company. Sacha mentioned a recent project that had kept her late most nights; Stan listened with the same quiet attention he had always given her, though something steadier now sat behind it.
Camilla remained mostly silent, watching them both with that same detached interest, occasionally tasting the air as though cataloguing the residual Qi in the dish.
Eventually Sacha’s curiosity circled back. She kept her tone casual, almost offhand, but the questions carried a clear undercurrent of sisterly assessment.
After a few more exchanges she leaned slightly closer to Stan, lowering her voice just enough that it felt private while still remaining audible in the quiet room.
"So..." A teasing smile curved her lips. "Is she more than just a friend?"
Stan met her gaze without flinching. "She is, yes. The thing between us isn’t a normal relationship."
Camilla’s posture stiffened almost imperceptibly. A faint flush touched the tops of her cheeks before she turned her face away with deliberate coolness, chin lifting.
"Hmph." The single sound carried equal parts pride and reluctant acknowledgment. She did not correct him, nor did she look at either of them.

Sacha’s smile widened, thoroughly entertained by the reaction. "Not a normal relationship, you say?" She glanced between her brother and the composed, faintly reddened woman across from them, clearly filing the information away for future teasing. "Well... that’s one way to put it."
Stan smiled awkwardly beneath Sacha’s teasing, knowing look.
’Why do I feel like she’s misunderstanding all this...?’

’Well, I suppose I should have expected it. What else would one assume after walking into a room and finding two people of opposite genders together, especially when one of them is a woman as beautiful as Camilla?’
’And considering she’s my sister, I guess it makes even more sense that she’d jump to conclusions and assume Camilla and I are that close.’
’What would be her reaction when she discovered that the reality of all this is considerably more complicated.’
’Camilla and I are comrades because of the contract. It hasn’t even been that long since we met, so our relationship hasn’t advanced to that level yet.’
He glanced briefly toward Camilla.
’Although I did add her to my harem through the system, that was primarily for my safety. I still have a long way to go before I can truly make her mine.’
His thoughts paused for a moment.
Then, remembering everything that had happened since the previous night, a faint smile tugged at the corner of his lips.
’Though, judging by the changes I’ve seen in her since last night... I have a feeling that day might come sooner than I expected.’
Stan quickly suppressed the thought before Sacha could somehow read it from his expression.
’For now, it’s probably better if Sis doesn’t know any of that.’

The light, awkward tension settled over the table like a third presence, Sacha openly amused, Stan in thought and calmly unbothered, and Camilla staring pointedly toward the window as though the entire conversation had nothing whatsoever to do with her.
After a moment Sacha took another bite, still smiling. "You know, most people just say ’girlfriend’ or ’partner.’ ’Not a normal relationship’ or ’Comrade’ is a lot more dramatic."
Stan shrugged one shoulder. "It’s accurate."
Camilla’s voice came from the direction of the window, cool and slightly clipped. "There is no need to explain further."
Stan couldn’t help but smile seeing that she didn’t correct that, though he knew he might just be thinking too much and reading way too much into this, progress was still progress.
Meanwhile, in response to Camilla, Sacha raised both hands in mock surrender, though the amusement in her eyes only deepened. "Noted. Completely noted."
She returned her attention to the plate, but the quiet that followed was different now, less heavy, more charged with the soft crackle of unspoken questions.
Stan watched his sister eat with mild satisfaction. Camilla continued to study the city lights beyond the glass, the faint color still lingering high on her cheeks.
Outside the formal language and the careful distance, something had shifted. Sacha had been given just enough of an answer to keep her curious, and not nearly enough to satisfy her.

chapters.title: Chapter 398: Game Of Survival
paragraphs: Sacha finished the last bite of her meal, set her utensils down with a soft clink, and looked up. Stan sat with his usual calm composure; Camilla remained perfectly still, her expression carefully neutral, crimson eyes half-lidded as though the entire afternoon barely concerned her. The residual awkwardness from the earlier "not a normal relationship" exchange still lingered in the air like static.
Sacha rolled her eyes with clear exasperation. "Gosh. You two are so boring."
Before either of them could respond, she reached into her handbag and pulled out a familiar rectangular pack. The moment the colorful Uno cards appeared, Stan’s eyes widened in genuine recognition.
Sacha turned the pack toward Camilla with a small flourish. "Do you know this?"
Camilla studied the bright packaging for a second, then gave a slight shake of her head. "No."
Sacha let out a long-suffering sigh. "Boring..."
Camilla’s brows drew together slightly.
"I don’t believe my lack of knowledge makes me boring."
"It does today."
Stan couldn’t help but chuckle.
Camilla immediately glanced toward him. "You find this amusing?"
Stan straightened slightly. "No."
"You are smiling."
"I wasn’t."
"You were." Camilla saying this with an expressionless face made everything funnier without even intending to...
Sacha burst into laughter. "Okay, I already like this."

Camilla nodded. "I see."
Stan raised an eyebrow. "That’s the part you decided to question?
Camilla looked at him. "I am trying to understand the rules."
Sacha laughed. "Don’t worry. You’ll understand once we start."
She picked up another card.
"Oh, and there’s one very important thing you need to know."
Camilla’s attention shifted back to her. "What?"

"And if I don’t?"
"You draw two cards."
Camilla nodded. "That seems simple enough."

"Like what?"

"I don’t know what you’re talking about."
"I know that look."

Stan stared at her. "You absolutely would."
Camilla’s gaze moved between them. "Is this another rule of the game?"
"No," Stan said.

Sacha grinned and Stan sighed, knowing that something devilish was going through his sister’s mind
Camilla however, remained completely serious.
"I see."
"You don’t see anything," Stan muttered.
Sacha laughed, clearly pleased to have an audience and a potential new victim.
She gathered the cards back into the pack and shuffled them.
"Want to learn by playing? I promise we’ll go easy..."
Her eyes shifted toward Stan. "...at first."
Stan’s expression immediately became wary.
Camilla, however, simply studied the cards with quiet curiosity, the earlier stiffness in her posture easing just a fraction as something new and unfamiliar presented itself.
Sacha smiled. "It’s simple once you start, but it gets vicious fast. Especially when people start holding grudges over Draw Fours."

chapters.title: Chapter 399: A Different Stan
paragraphs: "It’s simple once you start, but it gets vicious fast. Especially when people start holding grudges over Draw Fours."
Sacha shuffled the cards with a practiced ease, a faintly mischievous smile already tugging at her lips.
She looked toward Camilla.
"Alright, since you’re new, I’ll let you join us. Come on, it’ll be fun."
Camilla’s crimson eyes narrowed slightly.
She had been watching Sacha carefully throughout the explanation, and by now, she had already understood what the woman was thinking.
She intends to destroy me.
It wasn’t difficult to figure out.

Sacha’s smile was far too innocent, and the glint in her eyes was unmistakably competitive. She had spent years playing this game with Stan, and Camilla could tell that she was already imagining how easily she would crush a complete beginner.
Camilla regarded the scattered cards for a moment, then gave a small, decisive shake of her head.
"No."
Sacha blinked.
"No?"
"You two siblings should play first."
Camilla gestured toward the cards. "I will join during the second round. By then, the skills I gain from observing should be sufficient to understand the game properly."
Her crimson eyes shifted toward the deck. "You two will not win after I learn the rules."
Sacha stared at her for a moment. Then a slow smile spread across her face. "Hmmm..."
She leaned back slightly. "Seems you overestimate your ability and underestimate my brother and me."
Camilla’s lips lifted slightly. "On the contrary, I think you’re the one underestimating me."
Sacha’s smile froze for a moment. "Oh?"
Camilla simply met her gaze. "I learn quickly."
Stan shook his head, already sensing the familiar spark of rivalry igniting between the two women.
"It’s all right. We’ll know who wins when we get there. It won’t be easy for either of you... after all, I’m here."
A matching glint appeared in all three pairs of eyes.
Stan turned to his sister with a mild smile. "All right, let’s play, Sis. You used to beat me at Uno when we were kids... but I promise you won’t be able to beat me now."
Sacha tilted her head, intrigued. "Interesting. Why do you think so?"
"I’m obviously not the same Stan you used to beat."
She laughed and shook her head. "And you think I’m the same Sacha? You’re not the only one who’s grown, Stan."
Stan only smiled and let the comment pass. ’That’s not what I meant... but whatever.’
What he had actually meant was simpler and far less explainable.

After becoming a cultivator, both his physical capabilities and his mental acuity had risen sharply. His perception, memory, and ability to process information had all improved far beyond what an ordinary person could achieve.
And there was one particular advantage that made a game like Uno almost unfair.

He could notice microscopic differences in the backs of the cards, tiny variations in print, texture, scratches, bends, and wear that an ordinary person would never notice. From those differences alone, he could reconstruct a working model of what remained in an opponent’s hand.
With enough observation, he could essentially identify a card without ever seeing its face.
He had no intention of explaining any of that to Sacha. That would ruin the fun.
Sacha slid the deck across the table toward him. "You shuffle and deal."
Stan accepted the cards with a quiet smile. ’You’re really giving me that?’
Letting him handle the deck was essentially handing him the win condition.

As his fingers moved through the cards with casual ease, his enhanced perception catalogued every minute difference across the backs. By the time the hands were dealt, he already held a near-perfect mental map of the distribution.
He kept his expression completely neutral. ’This is going to be much easier than she thinks.’
Sacha arranged her cards and glanced at him. "What are you smiling about?"
"Nothing."
"You’re definitely smiling."
"I just remembered something."
"What?"
"How much you used to enjoy beating me."
Sacha grinned. "And how much I enjoyed watching you lose."
Stan shook his head. "Enjoy it while you can."
Camilla watched the exchange silently.
She had already begun paying close attention to the way the siblings handled the cards.
They finished setting everything up. The first card was placed on the table. The game began.
For the first few turns, everything proceeded normally.

Sacha played confidently, quickly placing matching cards whenever she had the opportunity. Her style was aggressive, favoring quick elimination of high-value cards while holding onto special cards for moments when they could shift the game in her favor.
Stan played differently. He was relaxed. Measured. Almost casual.
He never seemed to rush his decisions, yet he always appeared to have exactly what he needed.
Sacha narrowed her eyes. "Why are you suddenly playing so carefully?"
Stan shrugged. "I’m thinking."
"You never used to think this much."
"Maybe I’ve improved."
"Or maybe you’re scared."
Stan smiled. "Keep telling yourself that."
Sacha clicked her tongue.
Camilla’s crimson eyes moved between them. She was already beginning to understand their dynamic.
They didn’t simply play against each other. They knew each other. Every expression, hesitation, and habit carried information.
Yet Stan seemed to be reading Sacha more easily than she was reading him.
A few more turns passed. Sacha drew a card. Stan’s eyes flicked toward it for less than a second.
He recognized the tiny crease near its upper corner.
’Reverse.’
Sacha placed another card instead.
Stan calmly responded with one of his own. The game continued.
Camilla noticed that Stan’s decisions seemed unusually precise.
Whenever Sacha attempted to change the color strategically, Stan somehow had an answer.
Whenever she appeared to gain momentum, he disrupted it.
And whenever she reduced the number of cards in her hand, he seemed to find a way to slow her down.
Camilla’s eyes narrowed slightly. ’He is controlling the flow of the game.’
Sacha was beginning to notice it too. "You’ve gotten annoying."
Stan smiled. "I’ll take that as a compliment."
"You shouldn’t."
Another turn passed.
Stan placed down a Draw Two.
Sacha stared at him. "Seriously?"
"Yes, I told you I’m not thesame Stan you beat in Uno few years ago."
"Hmmph, you’re just lucky..." She snorted and reluctantly drew two cards.
Camilla watched the exchange carefully. ’He waited until she had fewer cards before using it. Interesting.’
Sacha’s hand gradually became smaller again.
So did Stan’s.
Then Sacha suddenly smiled. "Oh?"
Stan looked up. She placed down another card.
"I think you’re in trouble."
Stan glanced at his hand. "Do you?"
"Absolutely."
Camilla watched Sacha’s expression. She was confident again.
But Stan remained completely calm. He placed down another card and said in a calm voice: "Draw Two."
Sacha’s smile disappeared, "You’re kidding."
Stan shook his head. "I’m not."
She drew the cards, glaring at him, "You’ve really changed."
Stan shrugged. "I told you."

"Looks like I’m finally catching up."
Stan said nothing.
She played another card. "One more."
Her hand dropped to a single card.
Sacha immediately pointed toward herself. "Uno!"
Stan smiled. "Good."
Sacha leaned back with a satisfied expression. "Looks like you’re finally going to lose."
Stan looked at her remaining card. He already knew what it was.
’Yellow seven.’ He glanced at his own cards. ’Perfect.’
He placed a Wild card onto the pile. "Yellow."
Sacha’s expression changed. "Wait..."
Stan calmly followed with another card.
Sacha stared at him. "You planned that?"
"Maybe."
She drew. Then another turn passed.
Stan continued controlling the colors, forcing her to draw whenever she couldn’t match the current card.
Camilla watched every move with increasing concentration.
He wasn’t merely playing his cards well. He knew what Sacha had. He knew which colors she lacked. And he was choosing his plays accordingly.
How?
She didn’t have enough information to determine the answer yet.
But she memorized the sequence.
Finally, Sacha was forced to draw again. Stan placed down his final card with a soft, decisive tap.
"Uno."
Sacha froze. Her eyes widened. She looked at his empty hand. Then at her own. Then back at him.
"...Impossible. You were actually able to defeat me."
Stan leaned back, raising one hand in a deliberately smug little gesture of victory, basking in the moment with zero shame.
"I told you.
Sacha’s face scrunched into a pout. "There won’t be a second time.
Stan smiled. "We’ll see."
From the side, Camilla’s calm voice cut in, cool and certain. "Yes. Indeed. There won’t be a second time... not only for him, but for you as well, friend."
Sacha’s head snapped toward her.
She grit her teeth, competitive fire flaring. "You think you can beat me the way my brother did? You’re just a newbie. You didn’t even know what this game was a few minutes ago."
Camilla only met her gaze with serene confidence, the faintest hint of a smile still playing at the corner of her mouth. "I have spent the entire game observing."
Sacha crossed her arms. "Observing isn’t the same as playing."
"I disagree." Camilla’s eyes moved briefly toward the scattered cards. "You both have patterns."
Sacha’s expression changed slightly. "Patterns?"

"You hesitate before certain plays. You favor particular cards when specific colors are available. You also react differently when you are confident and when you are attempting to deceive the other player."
Stan raised an eyebrow.
Camilla continued calmly. "I have memorized them."
Silence fell and Sacha blinked, a bit dumbfounded.
Stan shook his head, holding back a smile, mildly amused by his sister reaction...
Then Sacha slowly turned toward her brother. "Brother..."
Stan cleared his throat. "Yeah?"
"I think we may have created a monster."
Stan looked toward Camilla. Camilla’s faint smile remained.
For the first time since the game had begun, Stan felt a genuine sense of danger.
’She’s actually serious.’
And somehow, that only made the second round feel even more interesting.
The air between the three of them crackled with fresh challenge as the cards were gathered for the next round.
Anyways, Sacha pulled the scattered cards toward herself with a decisive motion.
"You’re the newcomer," she said, giving Camilla a sharp little smile, "so I’ll make this fair. I’ll deal."
Camilla inclined her head once, unbothered. "Very well."

Stan watched as his sister shuffled with practiced speed. He could see the dual purpose in her movements. She genuinely wanted the game to feel fair for a first-time player, yet the competitive glint in her eyes made it clear she also intended to test just how far this composed stranger could go.
Camilla, for her part, tracked every motion of Sacha’s hands and the shifting deck with quiet, laser-like focus.
She’s actually studying the shuffle, Stan noted, mildly impressed.
Sacha dealt the hands. "One, two, three...
She distributed the cards around the table before finally dealing the last few to herself.
Camilla accepted each card without immediately looking at it.
Sacha noticed. "You’re not checking your cards?"
"I will when you’re finished."
Sacha raised an eyebrow. "Confident."
"I simply don’t see the need to rush."
Stan smiled faintly. She’s definitely taking this seriously.
Once the final card had been dealt, Camilla picked up her hand and arranged the cards neatly.
The second round began under a completely different atmosphere than the first.

Sacha no longer carried the easy confidence of someone who expected to dominate. Stan remained relaxed, certain he understood the flow of the game better than either of them. Camilla sat perfectly composed, posture straight, expression calm.
There was not a trace of first-game nerves on her face.
Sacha noticed.
Why isn’t she nervous? She literally learned this game less than half an hour ago.
She glanced at Stan. He looked just as calm. That realization sat uncomfortably in her chest.
’Seriously?’
At that moment, both of them were already treating Camilla like a legitimate opponent.
Sacha clicked her tongue lightly. "Alright. Enough talking. Let’s play."
She placed the first card down. The game opened.
Sacha waited for the beginner mistakes. Hesitation, wasted action cards, poorly timed color changes. They never came.
Camilla examined the discard pile, her own hand, and the previous plays with measured care before each decision. She did not rush, yet she never stalled.
Early on, she discarded high-value cards that would become burdens later. She held useful action cards in reserve. She refused to change colors unless the shift clearly benefited her position.
When Sacha tried to steer the available colors, Camilla simply adjusted.
More than once she seemed to anticipate what remained in the other two hands based purely on what had already been played.
Sacha’s unease grew. ’She’s not playing like someone who just learned the rules.’
And just like that a few turns passed.
